commits.pr_title: [Feat][Frontend] Add Watchdog for Engine and Worker Monitoring
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

 Fixes RFC [#56816 ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56816)

  Add a watchdog mechanism to vLLM V1 to automatically capture all-thread stack
  traces when the engine or worker process stops making progress, making it easier
  to diagnose hangs and deadlocks.

  - **New `vllm/utils/watch_dog.py`**: introduces the `WatchDog` class. A background
    daemon thread monitors a heartbeat (`feed()`); if the heartbeat is not refreshed
    within a timeout (default 300s, checked every 10s), it dumps the stack traces of
    all threads via `faulthandler` into a per-process log file
    (`VLLM_STACK_DUMP_for_<name>_<pid>.log`). Repeated timeouts without an intervening
    feed are logged only once. Provides `feed()` / `dump_stack()` / `start()` /
    `stop()` and a process-wide singleton `get_watch_dog()`.
  - **EngineCoreProc**: creates and starts a watchdog named `engine` after startup and
    feeds it while processing the input queue and before each engine step. The input
    queue `get()` now uses `timeout=5` so the loop stays responsive while preserving
    the original blocking semantics. The shutdown signal handler dumps all thread
    stacks for diagnosis.
  - **WorkerProc** (multiproc executor): likewise creates and starts a watchdog named
    `worker` and feeds it before executing every worker method; its signal handler
    dumps all thread stacks.


  ## Test Plan & Result

### Test Qwen3-8B by TP 1:

- Launch vllm:

```
vllm serve /mnt/weight/Qwen3-8B/ \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --gpu_memory_utilization 0.80 \
  --max_num_seqs 32 \
  --served_model_name qwen \
  --dtype float16 \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": false}}' \
  --enforce-eager \
  --max_model_len 20480 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --watchdog-config '{"timeout": 30, "check_interval": 5, "dump_dir": "/home/w00556288/log"}' 
```

- Construct feed timeout by patching
- Dump result:

```
(EngineCore pid=842) INFO 09-11 16:19:51 [watch_dog.py:51] [Watchdog]Dumped stack to /home/w00556288/log/VLLM_STACK_DUMP_for_engine_0_842.log due to feed timeout
```

### Test Qwen3-8B by TP 2:
- launch vllm:

```
vllm serve /mnt/weight/Qwen3-8B/ \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --gpu_memory_utilization 0.80 \
  --max_num_seqs 32 \
  --served_model_name qwen \
  --dtype float16 \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": false}}' \
  --enforce-eager \
  --max_model_len 20480 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --watchdog-config '{"timeout": 30, "check_interval": 5, "dump_dir": "/home/w00556288/log"}' 
```

(Worker_TP1 pid=1499) INFO 10-19 11:27:47 [watch_dog.py:51] [Watchdog]Dumped stack to /home/w00556288/log/VLLM_STACK_DUMP_for_worker_1_1499.log due to feed timeout
(Worker_TP0 pid=1498) INFO 10-19 11:27:47 [watch_dog.py:51] [Watchdog]Dumped stack to /home/w00556288/log/VLLM_STACK_DUMP_for_worker_0_1498.log due to feed timeout

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Add derender output mode to generate
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `output_mode="derender"` to `/inference/v1/generate`, so the generate server returns the parsed assistant message itself. This is Phase 2 of #56851 and builds on #60073.

## Claims

- `output_mode="derender"` returns `message` (content, reasoning, tool calls) on every choice without a separate `/derender` call
- `message`, `finish_reason` and `logprobs` match coupled `/v1/chat/completions` even for parsers whose `adjust_request` changes decoding. `/derender` can't match those
- `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/messages/render` now return `parse_context`. Other output modes ignore it, including fields added by a newer render, so prefill legs don't change
- A bad `parse_context` gets a 400 before generation. When a parser hides the reasoning, `token_ids` are dropped along with logprobs, like coupled chat
- Batch `/derender` now supports `parallel_tool_calls=false`, like coupled chat

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py -v 
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -v 
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py -v 
```

The parity tests run R1-Distill with hermes and deepseek_r1 against coupled chat. They cover plain output, reasoning shown and hidden, `tool_choice` auto, required and named, `parallel_tool_calls=false`, a stop string, `n=2` and logprobs with `top_logprobs=3` and `logprob_token_ids`. Every case checks `finish_reason` and the tool call ID shape.

## Details

The derender level parses the engine's own `output.text`. That text already has the stop string cut and was decoded with the flags `adjust_request` set which is where `/derender` drifts from coupled chat (#42729).

- **Chat context.** `/render` puts a `ParseContext` on the `GenerateRequest` with the tools, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `include_reasoning`, resolved `chat_template_kwargs` and the history tool call count. It's only read when `output_mode="derender"`. I went with always sending it, rather than only on request, so a rendered request works as is (decision 2 on #56851). `parse_context` is validated in `serve_tokens` before the request reaches the engine. Unknown fields fail the request only when `output_mode="derender"` because that's the only level that reads them. At the other levels they're logged once and ignored, so an older generate node keeps serving a newer render. `chat_template_kwargs` is typed as JSON values to make sure whatever goes in it has to survive the wire. The trade-off is that every rendered request carries the tools list, prefill legs included.
- **Parsing.** The generate server builds a slim `ChatCompletionRequest` from `parse_context` and reuses `_parse_and_assemble` from #60073. `/render` resolves the template kwargs once and uses them for both `reasoning_parser_kwargs` and `parse_context`. A handler can pass its `_engine_chat_template_kwargs` to keep API server only state out of `parse_context`. Cohere uses this for `_position_to_source` and friends. Tool call IDs keep the parser's `tc.id` (#61852).
- **`finish_reason`** goes through `resolve_finish_reason` (#59324), the same as coupled chat and batch `/derender`.
- **Logprobs** are chat shaped and cut with `chat_top_logprobs_limit` (#59518). They're on whenever `num_logprobs` is set, so `logprob_token_ids` works. When a parser hides the reasoning, `logprobs` and `token_ids` are both dropped. The tokens and text levels don't  change.

Limitations:
- Streaming returns a 400 for now. That's Phase 3.
- The `text` level still ignores `logprob_token_ids`. That gap was already there.
- #57442 and #60915 add logprob flags this level can't support. Neither is on `main` yet, so there's a TODO and whichever PR lands second adds the 400.
- Cohere citations from the derender level come back without document sources. The position-to-source map can't go over JSON.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --custom-histogram-buckets
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python's `--custom-histogram-buckets` (vllm-project/vllm#48867) replaces the default bounds of a bucket family across all of its histograms. The Rust frontend rejects the flag at startup (placeholder from vllm-project/vllm#62431) and hardcodes the bucket lists per histogram. This PR implements it with the same families and validation as Python.

## Claims

- `--custom-histogram-buckets '{"time_to_first_token": [0.5, 1.0], ...}'` now starts the Rust frontend, and every histogram in a listed family exports the custom bounds; unlisted families keep their defaults. It works under `vllm-rs serve` and through `--args-json`.
- Keys and bounds are validated like `ObservabilityConfig.custom_histogram_buckets`: known family names, non-empty, finite, > 0, strictly increasing, no booleans. Invalid input fails startup.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2225 tests run: 2225 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `custom_buckets_replace_listed_family_defaults` renders a fresh registry: listed families (`time_to_first_token`, `inter_token_latency` through `request_time_per_output_token_seconds`, `request_tokens` without a `max_model_len`, and the scheduler's `kv_cache_residency`) use the custom bounds, and an unlisted one keeps its defaults. `custom_buckets_are_validated_like_python` pins the errors. `custom_histogram_buckets_reach_frontend_config` checks both launch paths and that invalid bounds fail startup. The existing `request_token_buckets_are_capped_at_max_model_len` still passes.

## Details

`vllm-metrics` owns the buckets of its histograms, so the family table and its validation live there, in a new `buckets` module mirroring `vllm/v1/metrics/buckets.py`:

- The default lists, moved verbatim from `request.rs` and `scheduler.rs`.
- `BucketFamily`, keyed like `BucketFamilyKey`, and `CustomHistogramBuckets`, which validates on deserialization.
- A `FamilyHistogram` constructor per family that reads one shared `BucketConfig`: custom bounds when the family is listed, else the defaults. It replaces `RequestTokensHistogram`, whose deferred `max_model_len` cap moves into the same config; a custom `request_tokens` list does not need `max_model_len`, as in Python.

The registry is process-global and built lazily, so the bounds are fixed after construction and before first use, the pattern `set_max_model_len` already uses: the server, which owns startup ordering, calls `Metrics::set_custom_histogram_buckets` at the start of `build_state`, before the engine connection can record anything. The CLI only parses JSON into that type. Histograms outside the families (HTTP duration, Mooncake, NIXL) keep their own buckets, as in Python. The flag is not forwarded to the managed engine under `vllm-rs serve`, since only the frontend logger reads it.

- `CustomHistogramBuckets` implements `Eq` by hand so `SharedRuntimeArgs` keeps deriving it; validated bounds are finite, so equality is reflexive.
- Open Python PRs vllm-project/vllm#59807 and vllm-project/vllm#59808 would allow a 0 bound for count families; the Rust check mirrors current `main` and would follow.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR implements this flag in Rust.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Point users at --disable-flashinfer-autotune
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #61479, `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` is the advertised way to turn off FlashInfer autotuning. Docs, recipes, tests and eval configs still mostly show `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` or `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'`, so that is what people copy. This switches them to the advertised flag.

## Claims

- **Help text:** `--enable-flashinfer-autotune, --disable-flashinfer-autotune` now says what autotuning does, that it is on by default except at `-O0`, and that disabling it speeds up startup.
- **Startup logs:** both autotune cache log lines (managed v2 cache and per-rank cache file) mention `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`.
- **Docs:** `docs/design/optimization_levels.md` uses the CLI flags in the `-O0`/`-O1` settings and mentions `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` under "Startup Time Too Long".
- **Recipes and eval configs:** model recipes (DeepSeek, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, GLM-5.3, Inkling) and GSM8K eval configs use `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` instead of `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` / `--kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=False`.
- **Python tests and benchmarks:** these use the top-level `enable_flashinfer_autotune=False` kwarg instead of `kernel_config={...}`.
- **No behaviour change:** the old spellings still parse.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.
- On the rebased branch:

  | serve args | `enable_flashinfer_autotune` |
  | --- | --- |
  | `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` | `False` |
  | `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` | `False` |
  | `--enable-flashinfer-autotune` | `True` |

  `vllm serve --help=flashinfer-autotune` shows the new help text.
- Before the rebase, `tests/compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp1_quant.py -x` on a B300 had 63 passed and 0 failed through 79% of the file, then my 45-minute GPU reservation timed out. Those test edits are unchanged by the rebase.
- Not run locally: `tests/compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp2_ar_rms.py`, the two `test_sharded_sampling.py` files, `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py`, the GSM8K evals and the recipes. Their only change is the flag spelling, and both spellings parse identically.

## Details

`EngineArgs.create_engine_config` copies the top-level `enable_flashinfer_autotune` into `KernelConfig`, so all spellings are equivalent. In the `fusions_e2e` tests, dropping the explicit `kernel_config` dict lets the conftest default `{"enable_jit_warmup": True}` apply, which matches what the dict form produced before.

`tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_colpali.py` keeps the `kernel_config` form on purpose. It goes through `VllmRunner`, whose default `kernel_config` disables JIT warmup, so switching it would change the test's behaviour.

Other `--no-` spellings in recipes, such as `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, are out of scope here.

On making autotune off by default (raised in review): I'd keep it on. Autotuning picks noticeably faster kernels, and the aim is to make it cheap enough that people rarely need to turn it off.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `flashinfer autotune` and `enable-flashinfer-autotune docs`. The open autotune PRs (#59698, #61403 and others) change autotune behaviour, not how the flag is documented. Follow-up to #61479.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Preserve target-token scoring rows during DeepSeek-V4.1 replay
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes #62651 by retaining every prefill row for `prompt_logprob_token_ids` requests during DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder replay. Generation requests in the same batch continue to trim normally.

Strengthens the existing `test_prompt_logprobs_requests_keep_their_rows` test without adding test functions or collected pytest cases relative to the PR base. It exercises request registration, ordinary and target-token scoring, late scoring offsets, one- and two-chunk prefill, non-identity request-slot mappings, eager and piecewise replay preparation, exact gather/scatter outputs, and slot reuse by generation. The standalone target-scoring test and its Buildkite entries have been removed; existing CI already runs the replay suite.

## Validation

On GCP GB200, using the same environment for the PR base and revised tests:

- Existing replay batch and replay start suites: **15 passed**.
- Three replay suites combined: **22 collected, 19 passed, 3 failed**, both on the PR base and after this revision. The same three `test_replay_graph_matches_eager` cases fail: the first hits a PyTorch `CachingHostAllocator` internal assertion during CUDA Graph capture, and the remaining two report nested graph capture. These environment failures remain unresolved.
- Regression check with the production fix removed: the strengthened existing test **fails**, detecting 172 missing scoring rows; it passes with the fix restored.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks: **passed**.

Commands (with this checkout and a task-local `humming-kernels==0.1.17` dependency directory on `PYTHONPATH`; native extensions reused from the server installation):

```bash
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py -q
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py -q
# Repeat with the production fix temporarily removed:
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py::test_prompt_logprobs_requests_keep_their_rows -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py \
  .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml
```

This updates the existing fix in #62652 rather than opening a duplicate PR. AI assistance was used for the test refactor and validation. The production fix is unchanged by this revision. These component tests use synthetic layer outputs; they do not establish full-model accuracy or end-to-end model execution.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Reject multimodal inputs in chunked embeddings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reject multimodal embedding requests when enable_chunked_processing is enabled, instead of silently dropping their multimodal data. Return HTTP 400 with guidance to disable chunked processing.

## Claims

- Reject multimodal inputs, including short inputs, before chunk expansion or inference submission.
- Preserve text-only chunked processing and multimodal requests with chunked processing disabled.

## Validation

uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_protocol.py -q

72 tests passed. Added coverage for short and long multimodal inputs in mixed batches, plus the disabled-setting case. Applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Real HTTP validation used google/siglip-base-patch16-224 on an H800, BF16, eager mode, max_model_len=64, and max_num_seqs=1:

- With chunking enabled, image requests through /v2/embed and mixed text/image batches through /v1/embeddings returned HTTP 400. Subsequent text requests succeeded.
- With chunking disabled, image and mixed-batch requests succeeded; red and blue images produced different embeddings.
- A 217-token text input was split into four chunks. Its aggregated embedding matched the independently computed weighted, normalized reference within a maximum absolute difference of 3.31e-8.

## Details

maybe_pre_process_chunked() rebuilds inputs using tokens_input(), which discards multimodal payloads, hashes, and placeholders, even when the input fits in a single chunk.

This change validates the entire batch before rewriting inputs, preventing silent multimodal data loss when chunked processing is enabled.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] HY4 preview perf boost
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Improve the performance of HY 4 preview FP8 on ROCm platform. What this PR contains:

1. Enable AITER MoE for HY4 FP8. Actually AITER FP8 MoE already supports Silu activation, so we just change the vLLM side code to utilize it;
2. Rewrite iHC kernels with Triton to replace the default PyTorch impl (with fusions);

## Test Plan
**Server side:**
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8  \
  -tp  8 \
  --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --moe-backend aiter

**Client side:** 
vllm bench serve \
  --model tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8  \
  --host localhost \
  --port 8000 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 \
  --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-warmups 5 \
  --num-prompts 100 \
  --max-concurrency 32

**accuracy:**
lm_eval \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --tasks gsm8k \

commits.pr_title: [CI][KV Connector] Start NIXL accuracy decoders after prefillers on shared GPUs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix `:nvidia: (L4) NixlConnector PD accuracy core`. It has failed on every main build since 96279 and also hits PR builds, e.g. [96345](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96345#01a15d7b-d2e0-44fb-af42-73adadf13e22). It failed intermittently in an earlier stretch too (96041 to 96139).

The failing config is `DP_EP=1 GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.4 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=1 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`:

```
(EngineCore) Model loading took 6.29 GiB memory
(EngineCore) Available KV cache memory: -2.34 GiB
ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks.
(Worker_DP1_EP1) AssertionError: Error in memory profiling. Initial free memory 14.91 GiB, current free memory 17.29 GiB.
```

**Root cause:** a startup race on a shared GPU. The L4 step has 2 GPUs. The prefiller gets GPU 0, and the decoder (DP=2) gets `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0`, so decoder rank 1 wraps onto GPU 0. All servers launch at once. If the decoder loads its weights while the prefiller is profiling, the prefiller counts the decoder's 4 GiB as its own usage, and its 0.4 × 22 GiB budget goes negative. The decoder's "Error in memory profiling" is a follow-on: the prefiller dies and frees GPU 0 in the middle of the decoder's own profiling.

Nothing changed in the memory footprint between pass and fail. Prefiller weights are 6.29 GiB and the decoder takes 4.04 GiB per rank in both. Only the timing changed: the prefiller load took 10.7 s in passing 96249 and 17.5 s in failing 96279.

| | 96249 (pass) | 96279 (fail) |
|---|---|---|
| Prefiller model load | 6.29 GiB, 10.7 s | 6.29 GiB, 17.5 s |
| Prefiller available KV cache | 1.92 GiB | −2.34 GiB |
| Decoder model load per rank | 4.04 GiB | 4.04 GiB |

**Fix:** when the instances need more GPUs than the host has (so some GPUs are shared), wait for the prefillers to be ready before launching the decoders. Configs with dedicated GPUs keep launching everything in parallel. The prefiller is then steady when the decoder profiles, so the decoder correctly sees the prefiller's reservation as already used, and 0.4 × 22 GiB still fits in the remaining free memory.

**Not a duplicate:** #62806 changes how a worker reacts when another process frees memory during profiling, which is the decoder-side symptom. It doesn't stop the prefiller's budget going negative. #62568 restructures the sweep into pytest but keeps concurrent startup.

## Test Plan

- `bash -n` and shellcheck (pre-commit) pass.
- Not run on a GPU locally. The `(L4) NixlConnector PD accuracy core` step will confirm.

commits.pr_title: [XPU] Enable spec-decode adaptive verification without a confidence head
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

PR #52228 provides support adaptive verification without a confidence head and this PR enable it for XPU path. We identified perf gap caused by FA kernel and can be addressed by PR [647](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/647)(Not block current enablement). With these 2 PRs, we got below bench results:

## Performance Summary

Benchmarked Muse-Glimmer-30B + DFlash2 on **8 Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs (TP8)**,
comparing adaptive verification enabled/disabled at K=3/5/7.

Server launch:
```
ADAPTIVE=true

"${VLLM[@]}" serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name "$MODEL" --port 8000 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config "{
    \"method\":\"dflash\",
    \"model\":\"z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2\",
    \"attention_backend\":\"FLASH_ATTN\",
    \"num_speculative_tokens\":${K},
    \"draft_sample_method\":\"probabilistic\",
    \"enable_adaptive_verification\":${ADAPTIVE}
  }"
```

Output throughput change with adaptive verification enabled, relative to
disabled at the same K:

| Workload | K3 | K5 | K7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SPEED, high entropy, BS24 | -2.59% | +5.40% | +6.25% |
| SPEED, low entropy, BS24 | -4.99% | +3.81% | +2.21% |
| Sonnet, BS32 | -3.18% | +11.10% | +11.70% |

- **SPEED:** 12 configurations, 512 requests/configuration, 512 output
  tokens/request. Adaptive verification improves K5/K7 throughput, while K3
  without adaptive remains the fastest measured configuration.
- **Sonnet:** 6 configurations, 96 requests/configuration, 2048 output
  tokens/request. K5 + adaptive achieves the highest throughput
  (**468.55 tok/s**), 2.80% above K3 without adaptive. Mean E2E latency decreases
  by **8.17% at K5** and **10.98% at K7** versus their respective disabled controls.
- All **6,720 requests succeeded**, with zero failures.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Enable batch invariance for eagle3 scheduling accuracy
commits.pr_body:
## Summary
Enable `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` on ROCm for the eagle3 async-scheduling accuracy test.
ROCm hipBLASLt may select different GEMM solutions depending on batch shape. This can introduce small numerical differences between synchronous and asynchronous scheduling, changing near-tie greedy tokens and eagle3 acceptance rates.
The same issue was previously fixed for the ngram speculative-decoding test in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62048. That change enabled batch invariance for ngram, but the eagle3 test was not covered.
This change factors the existing ROCm setup into a shared helper and applies it to both eagle3 and ngram tests.

## Testing
Enabling `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` selected `TRITON_ATTN` and exercised the batch-invariant Triton matmul implementation. Under this configuration, the synchronous baseline and both non-preemptive asynchronous configs produced bit-identical eagle3 acceptance rates across all sampling parameter sets.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Apply response_format over structured_outputs like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python applies a non-`text` `response_format` on top of `structured_outputs` (`structured_outputs_from_response_format`, `vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/protocol.py`, used by chat and completions). The Rust frontend returns `structured_outputs` as soon as it is present and ignores `response_format`. This PR merges the two like Python.

## Claims

On `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` with both fields set, the Rust frontend now behaves like Python:

- Same constraint kind (for example `structured_outputs: {"json": ..., "disable_any_whitespace": true}` with a `json_schema` response format): the `response_format` constraint wins, and the `structured_outputs` options (`disable_any_whitespace`, `disable_additional_properties`, `whitespace_pattern`) and backend are kept. Before, the request ran with the old schema.
- Different kinds (for example `structured_outputs: {"regex": ...}` with `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}`): 400 with Python's message, "You can only use one kind of structured outputs constraint but multiple are specified." Before, the request silently ran with the regex.
- `response_format` of type `text`, or absent: `structured_outputs` unchanged.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2225 tests run: 2225 passed, 13 skipped
```

- New unit tests next to `convert_from_response_format`: a same-kind override keeps the options, `text` keeps `structured_outputs`, and a different kind is a 400. The override and conflict tests fail on the base.

## Details

Python uses `dataclasses.replace`, which overrides the field of the same kind and leaves a field of another kind in place; `StructuredOutputsParams.__post_init__` then rejects two constraints. `convert_from_response_format` (`rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/utils/structured_outputs.rs`) is already the one place that lowers both DTO fields into `StructuredOutputsParams` for chat and completions, so the merge lives there: it compares the constraint kinds and either replaces the constraint or rejects the request. The completions variant (`convert_from_response_format_value`) now delegates to it instead of returning `structured_outputs` first. The merged params are validated as before when `response_format` contributed, so a `response_format` schema still gets its nesting and xgrammar checks.

One deliberate difference: a malformed `structured_outputs` constraint that `response_format` would override (`structured_outputs: {"json": "{"}` plus a valid `json_schema`) is still a 400, because `structured_outputs` is validated when it is deserialized. Python accepts it only because `dataclasses.replace` drops the old value before anything reads it.

Not a duplicate: vllm-project/vllm#47176 (inactive since 2026-10-01) adds structured-output validation in the same file, but does not change how `response_format` combines with `structured_outputs`.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Carry return_token_ids through render like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since vllm-project/vllm#62449, Python's `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/completions/render` copy the request's `return_token_ids` onto the rendered `GenerateRequest` (`vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/render/serving.py`). The Rust frontend's `lower_render_request` (`rust/src/server/src/routes/render.rs`) always sets `return_token_ids: None`, so a client that asks render for token IDs gets none back from `/inference/v1/generate`. This PR carries the field through.

## Claims

- On the Rust frontend, render output carries the request's `return_token_ids`. Submitting it to `/inference/v1/generate` returns `prompt_token_ids` (and output token IDs), as on Python and as `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` do.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2222 tests run: 2222 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `render_completion_returns_generate_request_with_body_request_id` now asserts that render output carries the field, and the round trip `render_chat_response_can_be_submitted_to_generate_unchanged` asserts that generate echoes `prompt_token_ids` equal to the rendered token IDs. Both fail with the production change reverted.

## Details

The consumer is the generate route (`routes/inference/generate/convert.rs`), which already echoes prompt and output token IDs when `return_token_ids` is set; render only has to emit it. Both render handlers read the field from the request body and pass it to `lower_render_request`, which sets it next to the other request-level fields it copies (`stream`, `stream_options`, `cache_salt`).

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR changes the Rust render lowering.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL and VLLM_DISABLE_REQUEST_ID_RANDOMIZATION
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Python frontend reads two settings only from the environment: `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL` paces the periodic stats log, and the deprecated `VLLM_DISABLE_REQUEST_ID_RANDOMIZATION` keeps external request IDs as engine-core request IDs. The Rust frontend ignores both. This PR honors them on both launch paths.

## Claims

- `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL` (float seconds, `vllm/envs.py`) sets the Rust stats log interval, like Python's `asyncio.sleep(envs.VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL)` (`launchers/utils/server_utils.py`). Before, Rust always logged every 10s.
- `VLLM_DISABLE_REQUEST_ID_RANDOMIZATION=1` keeps the external request ID without the 8 random characters (`InputProcessor.assign_request_id`). Before, Rust always randomized.
- Both work under `vllm-rs serve` and under `vllm serve` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, with no Python change.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2227 tests run: 2227 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `serve_args_forward_env_only_settings_to_frontend_config` and `args_json_reads_env_only_settings_from_env` pin defaults, set values, `inf`, and errors on both launch paths; two table tests pin the parsers against Python's semantics; `stats_logger_runs_with_zero_interval` pins the zero-period guard and fails without it.

## Details

Environment handling stays in the CLI layer (`rust/src/cmd/src/cli.rs`), where `VLLM_API_KEY`, `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S`, and `VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE` are already read; the server and `vllm-llm` only see typed config.

- `vllm-rs serve`: clap binds each variable to a hidden flag (`env = ...`), as `--debug-cli` does with `VLLM_RS_DEBUG_CLI`. clap needs a long name to bind an env var; hiding it keeps the help aligned with Python, which has no such flag.
- `vllm serve` with the Rust frontend: `--args-json` is parsed with serde, so `apply_env_fallbacks` (formerly `apply_env_api_key_fallback`) reads both from the environment the Rust process inherits, like `VLLM_API_KEY`. It takes the environment lookup as a parameter so tests do not mutate process env.
- The values reach their existing consumers: `Llm::with_log_stats` takes the interval (`None` when stats logging is disabled or the interval never elapses) and passes it to `StatsLogger`; the server calls the existing `Llm::with_request_id_randomization`.

Parsing follows Python: `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL` ≤ 0 or NaN gives 10s; an interval too long for a `Duration` (`inf`, `1e30`) never logs, as Python's `asyncio.sleep(inf)` never wakes; `VLLM_DISABLE_REQUEST_ID_RANDOMIZATION` is `int(value) != 0`. Two differences: the stats logger rounds a zero interval (such as `1e-10`) up to 1ns, because tokio panics on a zero period; and a malformed value fails startup, while in Python it only kills the background logging task when that task first runs.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR touches these variables in Rust. Python's open vllm-project/vllm#45688 (inactive since 2026-07-29) proposes removing `VLLM_DISABLE_REQUEST_ID_RANDOMIZATION`; if it lands, the Rust side is one field and one builder call to drop.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support `--tokenizer`, `--tokenizer-revision`, and `--hf-config-path`
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend rejects `--tokenizer`, `--tokenizer-revision`, and `--hf-config-path` at startup, so a checkpoint that ships its weights without a tokenizer or config (for example a GGUF-only repo that borrows both from the BF16 repo) can only be served with the Python frontend. This PR supports all three options. It supersedes the community attempt vllm-project/vllm#57178, keeping its source mapping but restructuring the resolver instead of adding a second resolution path beside the existing one.

## Claims

- `vllm serve` (with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`), `vllm-rs serve`, and `vllm-rs render` accept the three options. The managed Python engine receives them too.
- Each group of files is read from the same source as in Python's `ModelConfig`:
  - tokenizer files and the chat template: `--tokenizer` at `--tokenizer-revision`, which defaults to `--revision`;
  - `config.json` and `generation_config.json`: `--hf-config-path` at `--revision`, and that source must contain `config.json`;
  - multimodal processor configs: the model.
- A weights-only model repo resolves from the HF cache, including offline, once the tokenizer and config come from elsewhere.
- Without the new options, resolution behaves as before.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo nextest run -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-managed-engine` passes: 1064 tests.
- New tests:
  - `resolved_model_files_read_each_group_from_its_source`: every file exists in all three dirs, and a snapshot records which dir each resolved file came from.
  - A model dir that holds only weights resolves with the overrides and fails without them.
  - `config.json` is required only for an explicit `--hf-config-path`.
  - The offline HF-cache test now covers distinct sources and a cache miss on the config source.
  - CLI coverage: `serve`, `frontend --args-json` (including `--tokenizer-revision` on its own), `render`, and the Python args forwarded to the managed engine.
- **Refactor check:** a temporary binary printed `ResolvedModelFiles` for 14 single-source cases, built once on `main` and once on each commit. The output was identical. Cases: a local dir; cached by branch and by commit SHA; offline misses; fresh downloads of `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` (tiktoken), `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3`, and `openai/gpt-oss-20b`; a missing repo.
- **Render check:** I took a GGUF-only checkpoint plus its BF16 sibling repo and ran `vllm-rs render` on the BF16 dir alone, then on the GGUF dir with `--tokenizer <bf16> --hf-config-path <bf16>`. The second run used both local paths and offline-cache HF ids. A tool-calling `/v1/chat/completions/render` request returned identical token IDs and sampling params (the `generation_config.json` defaults) in every case. Without the options, the GGUF dir fails with the same tokenizer error as `main`.
- Not run: GPU serving end to end. Only the frontend reads these files; the Python engine already accepted these options.

## Details

All model file access in the Rust frontend goes through `ResolvedModelFiles`. Its output fields stay unchanged, so its consumers don't change. The PR has three commits:

1. **Refactor, no behavior change.** `ResolvedModelFiles::new` had three resolvers (local dir, HF cache, Hub download), each repeating the full file list and its own tokenizer lookup. A private `SourceFiles` now replaces them. It is either a directory (a local dir or a cached snapshot) or a listed remote repo, and the struct is filled through it in one place.
2. **Feature.**
   - `ModelSource { id, revision }` and `ModelFileSources { model, tokenizer: Option, hf_config: Option }` (where `None` means "use the model"), plus `ResolvedModelFiles::from_sources`. Each field names the source it reads from.
   - A cached snapshot is used only if it contains the file that source must provide: the tokenizer file, `config.json`, or nothing for a model whose tokenizer and config both come from elsewhere. Today's rule, "the snapshot has a tokenizer", is the special case where everything comes from the model.
   - Server and render configs gain two typed fields, and the three `Unsupported` markers are removed.
3. **CLI grouping.** `model` and `--revision` move into the flattened `ModelArgs`, next to the new options. It lowers to one `ModelFileSources`, applying the Python defaults in one place, and forwards all four options to the managed engine.

Compared with vllm-project/vllm#57178, this avoids:

- a second resolution path with an early-return short-circuit;
- a third copy of the local/cache/remote resolvers;
- a source-equality matrix with a `require_config` flag;
- a cache-hit rule that accepts any one of five optional files;
- resolving the tokenizer source with the full resolver and discarding its config downloads;
- five positional string parameters;
- loose `Option<String>` fields threaded through every config.

Out of scope: a `model` that is a single `.gguf` file path (Python's `vllm serve x.gguf`). It still fails as an unknown repo id.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Report prompts over max_model_len like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A prompt longer than `max_model_len` fails on both frontends with a 400, but the Rust message differs from Python's and has no `param`. This PR reports it like Python: `This model's maximum context length is N tokens. However, your prompt contains M input tokens, which exceeds this limit even without any output tokens. Please reduce the length of the input prompt.` with `param: "input_tokens"` (`TokenizeParams._token_len_check`, `vllm/renderers/params.py`).

## Claims

- On the Rust frontend, a prompt over `max_model_len` returns Python's message and `param: "input_tokens"` on chat, completions, and generate. Before: `this model's maximum context length is N tokens, but the prompt contains M input tokens` with `param: null`. The message shares its `This model's maximum context length is` opening with OpenAI's own error, which clients match to detect a context overflow.
- A prompt that exactly fills the context gets the same opening and `param` with accurate wording ("your prompt fills it with N input tokens, leaving no room for output tokens").

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2222 tests run: 2222 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `prompt_too_long_maps_to_invalid_request` now snapshots the full error JSON of both variants, and `chat_wrapped_prompt_too_long_maps_to_invalid_request` checks the `param`. Both fail on the base.

## Details

The text layer owns the check (`resolve_max_tokens`, `rust/src/text/src/lower.rs`) and its errors. A new `vllm_text::Error::param()` accessor (delegated by `vllm_chat::Error::param()`) gives `input_tokens`, and the HTTP boundary (`server/src/error.rs`) puts it in the error's `param` instead of hard-coding one per route. `vllm_chat::Error::PromptTooLong` is removed: nothing constructs it, since the chat path wraps the text error.

- At `prompt_len == max_model_len`, Python's length check passes and the request then fails as `max_tokens must be at least 1, got 0.`. Rust keeps rejecting it up front, as before, now as `PromptFillsContext`, because "exceeds this limit even without any output tokens" would be false there.
- Python's HTTP message also ends with ` (parameter=input_tokens, value=M)`, which `VLLMValidationError.__str__` appends to every validation error. Rust reports `param` in its own field and appends it to no message, so that suffix is left out here too.
- gRPC maps the same validation errors to `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with the error text, so its message changes too.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR changes this Rust error.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Set the FP8 MLA prefill scale cache in the test double
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

`(MI355 DPX) Attention Kernels` fails every parametrisation of `test_fp8_prefill_matches_reference` with `AttributeError: 'AiterMLAImpl' object has no attribute '_fp8_prefill_one_scale'`. Both shards exit 1.

Failing step: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15124/list?sid=01a15db1-bcca-4faf-841f-646f5effa40b

## Cause

#59634 stopped allocating the FP8 dequant scale on every prefill call and cached it on the impl instead. `AiterMLAImpl.__init__` now stores `_fp8_prefill_one_scale = None`, and `_mla_fp8_prefill_attn` reads that attribute before filling it in.

The test never calls `__init__`. `_make_impl` builds the object with `object.__new__` and sets only the fields the forward used to read, so the new attribute does not exist and the read raises before any kernel runs. The test file was not updated in that PR.

Upstream CI does not catch this. The module is skipped everywhere except gfx950, and the upstream AMD `Attention Kernels` mirror runs on MI300. The only step that executes it is the internal `(MI355 DPX) Attention Kernels` job.

## Fix

Set `_fp8_prefill_one_scale = None` on the test double. That is the value `__init__` stores, and the forward already allocates the real tensor the first time it is `None`.

## Test plan

`pytest -v -s kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py` on MI355X. The module skips on every other arch, so this is the command behind the failing step.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO READ: await every read before the forward
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

MoRIIO READ loads KV synchronously (`load_kv_async=False`), so the decode worker posts every READ in `start_load_kv` and must not run the forward until they land. Main awaits all of them only when the forward context says FULL; otherwise it awaits only mamba/KDA reads and leaves attention to the per-layer `wait_for_layer_load` hook. Two cases fall through:

- **MRv2 FULL replay.** `pre_forward` runs before `run_fullgraph` with no forward context (`gpu/model_runner.py`), so `start_load_kv` sees mode NONE and awaits only KDA reads, and the per-layer hook never runs inside the graph. All attention-side reads (MLA, indexer K, kpool tail) can still be in flight when the graph consumes them. #60636 addresses this case by passing the FULL context.
- **PIECEWISE / eager.** Indexer caches (`DeepseekV32IndexerCache` and subclasses) never call `wait_for_layer_load`, so their reads are never awaited.

This PR awaits every READ posted in the step inside `start_load_kv`, in every cudagraph mode, and makes `wait_for_layer_load` a no-op (kept because the base method is abstract). Attention-only failures no longer stop the wait early, so one request's failure can't let the forward run on another request's in-flight reads; hybrid still fails fast and raises.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, 1P/1D MoRIIO READ, EP8, MTP 1, KV block 8, MI300X, default decode cudagraph mode (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE). Base: main `19b0efce30` + #60867 (needed to boot this model); "with" adds this PR.

**Race (instrumented, logging-only).** After each admission step's forward, a device sync, then a check of every READ the barrier did not await. Context length determines race likelihood: below ~32K reads usually land in time; above ~96K every admission races in the default recipe.

| context (tokens) | admissions racing without this PR | MLA / tail reads still pending after the forward | MLA bytes still pending, worst step | latest landing after the forward | with this PR: admissions / races | barrier wait with this PR (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ≤8K | 0 / 1306 | 0 / 0 | – | – | 2414 / 0 | 2–16 ms |
| 32K | 5 / 60 | 29 / 34 | 0.32 GB | 30 ms | 28 / 0 | 13–17 ms |
| ~100K | 4 / 4 | 8 / 0 | – | 17 ms | 8 / 0 | 33–64 ms |
| 256K | **36 / 36** | **359 / 420** | **3.0 GB** | **216 ms** | 63 / 0 | 73–155 ms |
| 512K | **3 / 3** | **33 / 36** | **5.0 GB** | 168 ms | 9 / 0 | 157–271 ms |
| ~713K | **3 / 3** | **35 / 36** | **8.0 GB** | 195 ms | 9 / 0 | 364–396 ms |

Without = main `19b0efce30` + #60867, default recipe (every admission replayed FULL), 4 runs on 2 node pairs; with = + this PR, default recipe plus forced PIECEWISE (21/3/3 of the 256K/512K/~713K admissions). Indexer K reads: 0 pending in every row. In 450/464 MLA cases the bytes the graph read differ from what the READ delivered afterwards (stale blocks from earlier requests). Forced PIECEWISE on main + #60636: 233 kpool tail reads consumed while still in flight (the indexer runs before the MLA hook); with this PR 0.

**Accuracy (same runs, without vs with).** Single-needle long-context probe (243K/486K/713K tokens × 3 depths) 9/9 vs 9/9, identical answers. GSM8K full 5-shot strict 92.04% ± 0.75 vs 92.42% ± 0.73. NIAH 96K words (3 seeds) 3, 1, 2 vs 1, 10, 10 (bimodal, not significant). We have not reproduced a wrong output caused by the race; the evidence is the pending-after-forward reads and the snapshots.

**Perf (c=1, same image with/without this change, same node pair).** Forced PIECEWISE 8K–512K: TTFT −1.8..+1.8%, ITL −3.4..+1.0% (same-build repeat spread: TTFT up to ~9% at 8K, ITL ≤1.8%). Default FULL_AND_PIECEWISE 32K–512K: TTFT +0.5..+1.4% (pair-to-pair spread 2–3%). Against #60636 on the same base: −0.3..+1.4% (noise 2–6%).

**Final head E2E.** Default recipe: 1242 admissions (all FULL replay), every READ awaited before the forward (104 per request), 0 MLA / indexer / tail reads pending after the forward; long-context probe 9/9; GSM8K 91.89% ± 0.75; no MoRIIO errors. Forced PIECEWISE: 32 admissions, 0 pending reads, probe 9/9. Barrier wait on admission steps (median): 150 ms at 256K, 271 ms at 512K, 364 ms beyond; ~3 ms for short prompts.

**Unit.** `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py` 36 passed; all `test_moriio_*.py` 256 passed (main 248), 260 stacked with #60867, 0 failed (ROCm nightly, MI300X). New tests fail on main / the previous head on their assertions. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, typos) passes.

> `pre-run-check` is the author merge-count gate, not lint; full CI runs once a maintainer adds `ready`.

## Details

**Tradeoff.** Steps that admit a transferred request outside FULL lose per-layer overlap; the added wait is bounded by the transfer tail that overlapped the forward. It is a host wait on RDMA completion statuses, no device sync, and only runs when the step has sync loads and posted reads. Steady-state decode is unchanged.

**Failure semantics.** Attention-only: the barrier waits for every request's reads (bounded by `transfer_timeout`) and failed requests are reported via `get_block_ids_with_load_errors`. Hybrid: fail fast and raise, since HMA load-error recovery is unsupported. A read still in flight when the barrier gives up (e.g. at `transfer_timeout`) fails the step closed in both modes.

**Relation to #60636.** Complementary. #60636 fixes the MRv2 FULL context; it does not cover indexer reads outside FULL. With both, FULL steps already await everything and this PR adds the non-FULL coverage.

## Checklist

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] Design fit: connector-only (`moriio_connector.py`, `moriio_engine.py`), +27/−84 non-test.
- [x] Testing and validation: unit + negative control, E2E race/accuracy/perf above.
- [x] Code quality: ruff, mypy, typos pass.

**AI assistance:** Claude helped with the investigation, implementation, tests, instrumentation and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Give the M3 embed-sharing fixture a kernel_config
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

`(MI355 DPX) V1 Executor + Worker` fails on every parametrisation of `test_m3_target_allocates_embedding_on_required_stage` with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'kernel_config'`.

Failing job: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15124/list?sid=01a15db1-bce5-4cd0-a3c0-f39c922bfb4b

## Cause

#62712 wired `specialized_decode_config()` into `MiniMaxM3Model.__init__` on the AMD path, and that helper reads `config.kernel_config.monokernel` unconditionally. The `m3_config` fixture in this test builds a fake `VllmConfig` as a `SimpleNamespace` and never carried a `kernel_config`, so the constructor now raises before the test reaches its assertion. Both halves are correct on their own; the fixture simply was not updated alongside the new call.

Only the AMD variant is affected, because the fixture imports `vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model` on ROCm and the nvidia model has no `specialized_decode_config` call.

The last upstream nightly passed because it started before #62712 landed, not because upstream is unaffected. The same group will fail there on its next run.

## Fix

Give the fixture a `kernel_config` with `monokernel` disabled, which is the real `KernelConfig` default, so the model falls back to the non-specialized path and the test keeps asserting exactly what it asserted before. This matches the fixture style already used by the DSv4.1 mono decode tests added in #60731.

## Test plan

`pytest -v -s v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py` on MI355X, which is the command behind the failing CI step.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Raise the bar for agent-written tests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Raise the bar for tests written by coding agents. Adds a 31-line `tests/AGENTS.md` with five rules that change what agents actually do, links it from `AGENTS.md` and `pr-checklist` §2.1, and rewrites the "unit over integration over e2e" line in `AGENTS.md`:

- **User-visible fixes need a real-path test** through `LLM`/`vllm_runner` or `RemoteOpenAIServer`, not only a unit test on hand-built inputs.
- **Show the failure before the fix**: run the new test on the base commit and paste the failing and passing output.
- **Never buy a green CI**: no reruns, retry loops, wider tolerances, lowered thresholds, skip, or deletion; check main first; `xfail` with an issue link for known bugs.
- **Deterministic by construction**: greedy/seeded sampling; vLLM is not batch invariant by default, so compare with `check_logprobs_close`/`check_embeddings_close` or require `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`; no fixed `sleep` as synchronization.
- **Make sure CI runs it**: a test no `.buildkite/test_areas/*.yaml` step selects never runs and looks like a pass.

## Validation

Fresh agents with no context got a repo path and one task, on `main` (old instructions) and on this branch.

| Task | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sampler bug that only shows up in a batch | CPU unit test only; e2e left as a manual repro in the PR text | unit test + committed `LLM` regression test with an exact assertion |
| Fix an issue (`echo=True, max_tokens=0` reports `completion_tokens=1`) | unit test feeding hand-built `RequestOutput` to the serving layer; e2e as a manual curl | regression test through the OpenAI server fixtures, streaming and non-streaming |
| New test fails intermittently | found the race, no retries | same, plus a negative check that the test fails without the fix |
| "CI is red, make it pass today" | refused to loosen the threshold | same, cites the rule; `xfail` + issue only if main also fails |
| vLLM vs HF / TP>1 bug | strong | strong; also caught that the only pooling CI step is single-GPU, so a TP=2 test would always skip |

The main difference is the first rule: on `main`, agents fix user-visible bugs with unit tests on synthetic inputs and leave the real path untested. `check_agent_files.py` reports no new problems (6 existing errors in `model-recipes` / `transformers-upgrade`).

## Details

The current rules come from #47784 and #57084; this replaces the "unit over integration over e2e" ordering instead of adding a conflicting rule, and keeps details in one place (`tests/AGENTS.md`). Prior art: sglang `.claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md` (regression tests fail before the fix, mock only boundaries), PyTorch review checklist (bug fixes need a reproducing test, `xfail` not `skip`), TensorRT-LLM `tests/AGENTS.md` (unregistered tests silently never run). Does not overlap the docs-requirement PR #62599.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend now supports `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none`. Before this change, it rejected the flag at startup. Its default handling of tools for `tool_choice="none"` now also matches the Python frontend.

## Claims

- `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none` works with `vllm serve` (including the Python→Rust `--args-json` handoff) and with `vllm-rs render`. When the flag is set and a chat completion request has `tool_choice="none"`, its request-level `tools` are left out of the prompt.
- **Default behavior change (now matches Python):** by default, request tools are rendered into the prompt even when `tool_choice="none"`. Before this change, the HF, DeepSeek (V3/V3.2/V4/V4.1), Harmony and Inkling renderers always dropped them, as if the flag were always on. Kimi K3 already matched Python. `tool_choice="none"` still disables tool-call parsing, and tool calls that a unified parser (Gemma 4, HunYuan, Inkling, Kimi K3, …) still recognizes are now dropped from the response instead of being returned as `tool_calls`, matching Python's parser engine.

## Validation

Qwen3-0.6B on GB200, `vllm serve --enforce-eager --max-model-len 2048`. The request has one tool and `max_tokens=1`; the table shows `usage.prompt_tokens`:

| frontend | flag | `tool_choice="none"` + tool | no tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`) | off | 127 | 9 |
| Python | on | 9 | 9 |
| Rust, main | off | 9 | 9 |
| Rust, main | on | fails at startup ("not implemented in Rust frontend") | – |
| Rust, this PR | off | **127** | 9 |
| Rust, this PR | on | **9** | 9 |

```bash
cd rust
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast
```

All tests pass except three that also fail on `main` or for environment reasons in my setup. None of them involve this change:
- `grammar_replay`: HF cache permission error while downloading DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- `roundtrip_gemma4_hf`: the locally cached tokenizer has no `response_template`. It fails on `main` too.
- `timing::tests::does_not_enable_debug_at_info`: order-dependent in a full workspace run and passes on its own. It is in the untouched `vllm-tracing` crate.

New and updated tests:
- `exclude_tools_only_drops_tools_for_tool_choice_none`: only an explicit `"none"` drops tools. `"auto"` and an unset `tool_choice` keep them.
- `chat_template_exposes_tools_to_templates_for_any_tool_choice`: the HF renderer passes tools to the template for both `auto` and `none`.
- `frontend_config_excludes_tools_when_tool_choice_none_from_args_json`: the flag survives the `--args-json` handoff from Python.
- `processor_excludes_request_tools_for_tool_choice_none_when_configured`: with the flag on, `none` drops only request-level tools and keeps developer-message tools; `auto` keeps both; without the flag, `none` renders both.
- `tool_choice_none_drops_tool_calls_parsed_by_unified_parsers`: a Gemma 4 tool call is returned for `auto` and dropped for `none`.

## Details

- **Where the flag is applied.** Python configures the flag on `OnlineRenderer` at construction and sets `tool_dicts = None` for `tool_choice == "none"`. Here it is likewise configured on `ChatRequestProcessor` at construction (like `tool_strict_level`) and applied right before rendering, so the chat-completions, `/render` and tokenize paths all get the same behavior. Request tools are still converted and validated; only request-level tools are dropped, and message-scoped tools are kept, as in Python. The server stores the setting in `Config`, and `vllm-rs render` in `RenderConfig`.
- **Dropping tool calls under `none`.** Unified parsers are built from the request tools regardless of `tool_choice`. Now that tools are rendered for `none`, a model may emit a call there, so structured assembly limits surfaced tool calls to zero for `none`, reusing the existing `parallel_tool_calls=false` limit (now `max_tool_calls: Option<usize>`).
- **Renderer change.** The renderers decided whether to render tools based on `tool_parsing_enabled()`, which is false for `tool_choice="none"`. Python's native renderers never look at `tool_choice` when deciding whether to render tools, so those gates are removed. Without that removal, the flag would have no effect for every renderer except Kimi K3.
- **Not duplicating existing work.** No open PR covers this flag. The other unsupported flags mentioned alongside it in the tracking note are out of scope here.
- **Follow-up.** The GPT-OSS cases in `test_serving_chat.py` start the server with this flag. Running them under the Rust frontend in CI would need a larger GPU than the current Rust e2e step uses, so this PR doesn't add them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Support simulated routing in monolithic MoE backends
commits.pr_body:
With `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`, monolithic TRT-LLM MoE backends can receive the vLLM-only `Simulated` routing enum (102), which FlashInfer does not implement.

Separate router identity from the routing method used by kernels. Backend selection now uses the model’s routing method, and the shared MoE runner asks the simulation router to generate random logits before monolithic execution. The router also supplies zero correction bias so learned biases do not skew simulated routing.

- Remove `Simulated` from the TRT-LLM FP8, MXINT4, and NVFP4 monolithic allowlists.
- Let each simulation strategy declare whether it supports generating monolithic logits; require a decomposed backend otherwise.
- Preserve ordinary router behavior when simulation is disabled.

Monolithic simulation retains the model’s routing algorithm, including expert grouping and weight calculation. Modular simulation continues to sample expert IDs directly with unit weights, so the two paths do not produce equivalent routing weights or expert combinations.

Added tests cover router contracts, factory selection, bias handling, shared-runner integration, and simulated routing capture with BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 monolithic kernels.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Share ChatStreamProcessor between chat streaming and derender
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Moves the per choice parse steps that chat streaming and parsed streaming derender both repeat into a shared `ChatStreamProcessor`. 

Closes #57572.

## Claims

- `OpenAIServingChat` streaming and `OnlineDerenderer._derender_chat_stream_parsed` now run the same code for `parse_delta`, `tools_streamed`, the `finish_reason` mapping and the parallel tool call filter
- The rule that hides logprobs and token IDs when reasoning is hidden lives in one place (`hide_metadata`)
- No change to what `/v1/chat/completions` streams

## Validation

Existing tests unchanged.

New unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_stream_processor.py`

No model eval needed since served output doesn't change.

## Details

The processor handles one choice. It takes a `Parser` instance rather than a class, so the `_make_parser` hook keeps working and the parser cache (#57571, #58417) can hold the processor. Each caller keeps its own extras. Serving keeps usage, logging and the chunked prefill skip. Derender keeps replay, detokenization, tool call ID pinning and `stream_state`.

Small differences:

- Derender: a choice that finishes without generating anything now sends an empty delta without calling the parser, same as serving
- With `parallel_tool_calls=false` the filter runs a bit earlier. Delta logs no longer show tool calls the client never gets and derender only records index 0 in `last_tool_call_ids`. Nothing streamed changes
