commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model][MiniMax-M3] Context-parallel sparse lightning indexer (Triton, opt-in)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Adds **context-parallel decode scoring** for MiniMax-M3's sparse lightning indexer on ROCm (TP>1, bf16 index cache, opt-in via `--attention-config '{"minimax_m3_indexer_cp": true}'`).

### Problem

MiniMax-M3 selects a sparse set of KV blocks per query token with a lightweight indexer that scores every block in the request's context. Index heads shard like KV heads (`sparse_num_index_heads == num_key_value_heads == 4`), and the index-K cache is a single shared head replicated on every rank. So with TP>1 every rank streams the whole index cache — the same `seq_len/128` blocks — once per decode step, just to score its own head(s). That read is duplicated `world_size` times and at long context and large decode batches it is a large term in the step.

### Solution

Shard the **blocks** instead of duplicating the read. Because each rank owns different index heads, every rank has to score every head on its shard:

1. All-gather the index queries — `heads * 128` bf16 per token (1 KB at M3's 4 heads).
2. Each rank scores **all global heads** on its `1/world_size` round-robin block shard (`block = local * world + rank`).
3. For each head, take the local top-k of the **full** `k` over the shard, pack each candidate into one int64 `(score, global block id)` key, and all-gather the keys — `P * heads * k * 8` bytes per token, independent of context length.
4. Merge per global head, keeping only the heads this rank owns.

Index-cache traffic per rank drops to `1/P`; scoring compute per rank is unchanged (`heads` heads over `1/P` of the blocks). The merge is exact: for a given head, a block in that head's global top-k is necessarily in its own shard's top-k for the same head. Forced init/sink and sliding-window blocks are pinned on both the shard and the merge.

**Default: OFF** (`AttentionConfig.minimax_m3_indexer_cp = False`); nothing enables it automatically. Turning it on is a startup error unless the index cache is bf16 (`indexer_kv_dtype` "auto" or "bf16") — the score kernel reads the cache without a scale; the fp8 path is #57909 — and when the fused decode path (#59653) is also enabled, since that kernel computes indexer top-k itself. It is also a startup error on non-ROCm platforms or with `tensor_parallel_size == 1`.

**When to enable:** long-context workloads. CP adds a fixed per-layer cost (two small all-gathers, scoring every index head, the merge), so it slows decode on short contexts and speeds it up on long ones. On MI350X at TP=4 (`vllm bench serve`, OSL 1024), mean TPOT changes by +15% / +7% at 4k ISL (concurrency 8 / 32), breaks even around 64k / 32k, and improves by 9% / 16–27% at 128k. TTFT is unaffected. Agentic traces (AgentX, ISL ~74k) fall on the winning side.

### CUDA graph capture

Two properties are required for CP to work under `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

**CP must be what gets captured.** vLLM v2 records FULL decode graphs with `cudagraph_runtime_mode=NONE` (see `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture`), so a `CUDAGraphMode.FULL` guard never fires. Guarding on `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` would record the **non-CP** indexer into the decode graph that is then replayed. The only guard is `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`, because Dynamo tracing cannot capture the collectives. Persistent buffers (in `IndexerCPDecode`) keep the decode path allocation-free so CP is what gets captured.

**Kernel shapes must be capture-stable.** Capture goes through `_dummy_run`, which sets `seq_lens = max_query_len`. Shapes derived from the batch's `max_seq_len` would specialize a one-block context into every decode graph. All kernel shapes come from `max_model_len`, and block counts and strides are runtime arguments rather than `tl.constexpr`. `test_indexer_context_scores_independent_of_shape_bound` asserts scores are identical whether the grid is sized for the batch or for a bound 8x larger.

`--enforce-eager` is not required.

### MiniMax-M3 sparse attention pipeline

| Stage | Backend | Index cache dtype | When selected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indexer | **Triton** (this PR) | `bf16` | `indexer_kv_dtype=bf16`; no AITER dependency |
| Indexer | AITER (#57909) | `fp8_e4m3` | `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8` |
| Attention | **AITER_SPARSE_PA** | — | `SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` + `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` |
| Attention | Triton | — | Fallback when AITER unavailable |

## Changes

| File | Type |
|---|---|
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — `IndexerCPDecode` (Q all-gather, per-head score/exchange/merge) and `MiniMaxM3IndexerTritonCPImpl` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — Triton `_context_score` shard kernel (bf16 cache only) |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/indexer_cp_exchange.py` | New — packed-key local top-k, all-gather (AITER IPC, RCCL fallback), per-head merge |
| `vllm/config/attention.py` | Modified — `minimax_m3_indexer_cp: bool = False`; rejects non-bf16 index caches and fused decode at startup |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py` | Modified — CP dispatch in `select_indexer_impl_cls` (ROCm, TP>1) |
| `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp.py` | New — shard scores, capture-shape invariance, per-head top-k merge (1 and 4 heads), head ownership |
| `tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp_tp.py` | New — multi-GPU CP vs non-CP top-k per global head |
| `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` | Runs the multi-GPU test in the AMD 4-GPU distributed job |

With `minimax_m3_indexer_cp` unset (the default) no existing code path changes.

## Test Plan

### Hardware and image
8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950). `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` with this PR's files applied on top of that exact commit.

### Correctness
```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp.py -v
pytest tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp_tp.py -v
```
The distributed test runs the production CP decode across real TP ranks and compares each rank's top-k with the non-CP decode kernel (`minimax_m3_index_decode`) on the full context, **per global index head**, using M3's config (4 heads, top-16, init 0, local 1) on 32k–82k token contexts. It is parametrized over TP 2/4/8 (TP=8 covers head replication), `query_len` 1/4 (spec-decode verify), and RCCL vs AITER IPC all-gather. It also asserts the four heads select different blocks on ≥90% of rows, so a merge that mixed heads would fail.

Contexts are deliberately long: at top-16 x 128-token blocks plus a forced local block, any prompt under ~2k tokens selects every block, so short-context evals cannot detect a wrong selection.

### Server (MXFP4 weights, Triton bf16 indexer)
Baseline is the same command without `"minimax_m3_indexer_cp":true`.
```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256

vllm serve /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --port 8779 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --language-model-only --enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"bf16","minimax_m3_indexer_cp":true}' \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking_mode":"enabled"}' --stream-interval 20 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

### AgentX benchmark
```
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp \
  --url http://localhost:8779 --endpoint-type chat \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k \
  --concurrency 32 --benchmark-duration 900 \
  --streaming --use-server-token-count \
  --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.0 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.0 \
  --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --tokenizer /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --apply-chat-template
```
aiperf 0.12.0, 900 s per point after a 90 s warmup.

## Test Result

### Correctness
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp.py`: 16 passed (including config validation).
- Server started with only `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"bf16","minimax_m3_indexer_cp":true}'` selects the CP indexer; the same flag with `"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"` exits at startup with the bf16 error.
- `tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp_tp.py`: 12 passed (TP 2/4/8 x `query_len` 1/4 x RCCL/AITER).

### AgentX sweep (MXFP4, TP=4, no speculative decoding)

Same node, same image, same PR code in both arms; only the CP switch differs. (These runs used the earlier environment-variable switch; it has since moved to `attention_config.minimax_m3_indexer_cp` with no change to the CP code path.) CP ran first, baseline second, then CP conc=15 was repeated on a fresh server. Every point has 0 failed requests.

| Concurrency | Baseline (tok/s/GPU) | CP (tok/s/GPU) | Throughput | Requests | ITL baseline → CP (ms) | ISL baseline | ISL CP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 12,652 | 12,997 | +2.7% | +1.6% | 16.2 → 14.7 (−9.5%) | 73,900 | 74,737 |
| 15 (repeat) | 12,652 | 13,320 | +5.3% | +3.3% | 16.2 → 13.8 (−14.9%) | 73,900 | 75,319 |
| 20 | 15,245 | 15,957 | +4.7% | +3.9% | 19.3 → 16.9 (−12.2%) | 75,343 | 75,935 |
| 24 | 15,385 | 17,115 | **+11.2%** | +7.7% | 22.7 → 19.7 (−12.9%) | 74,606 | 76,245 |
| 32 | 20,125 | 23,175 | **+15.2%** | +14.4% | 37.6 → 28.6 (−23.9%) | 73,741 | 74,232 |

The gain grows with decode batch size, as expected when the term being divided by `P` is per-sequence index-cache traffic. At concurrency 15 the throughput delta is about the size of run-to-run variation (baseline conc=15 measured 12,936 and 12,652 in two passes); ITL improves at every point. ISL is within 3% across arms with CP's the higher, so the delta is not a shorter-trajectory artifact.

One earlier pass on the same node was discarded: its baseline engine (CP off) exited partway through conc=32 (42% failed requests), and its CP conc=15 point ran at half speed with no errors. Neither reproduced in the pass above, which also logs both servers in full.

**Withdrawn:** the previous version of this PR scored only each rank's own index head on its shard and merged across ranks, which mixes different heads' candidates at TP=4. The AgentX, EAGLE3 and GSM8K results previously reported here were measured on that code and are removed. EAGLE3 has not been re-measured. GSM8K is not repeated because it cannot distinguish a correct selection from a wrong one at its context lengths (see Test Plan); the per-head equivalence test replaces it.

**Hardware note:** these are MI355X numbers; absolute tok/s/GPU is not comparable to the MI350X figures in earlier revisions. Every comparison is baseline vs CP on the same node.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance, including the per-head CP design, the CUDA-graph capture analysis, the multi-GPU equivalence test, and running the benchmarks above on our hardware, and was prepared with assistance from [PR Pundit](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/pr-pundit). I have reviewed every changed line and the results.

This does not duplicate #57909, which implements indexer CP for the **AITER fp8** path (`indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`). This PR covers the **Triton bf16** path. The two select different `MiniMaxM3Indexer` implementations and do not overlap in code.

## Related
- #57909 — CP indexer for the AITER fp8 path.
- #59653 — fused sparse-layer decode; CP is refused when it is enabled.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] MonoKernel decode for M3 MXFP4 on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
### Summary
Adds an opt-in specialized decode path (`--monokernel`) for MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on gfx950. During decode, layers 3–59 run their FFN half as one persistent FlyDSL launch:
- TP all-reduce, residual add and post-attention RMSNorm;
- the FP32 router with top-4 selection;
- the shared and routed BF16×MXFP4 experts;
- the final TP all-reduce.
Attention, the dense layers 0–2, prefill and mixed batches stay on the stock path.
- Follows the RFC #60904 / Kimi-K3 layout: `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/specialized_decode/`. There is one `plan()` per step, and layers are selected with `step.layer(i)`.
- Supports eager and FULL CUDA graphs, at 1–16 decode rows. Larger batches, PIECEWISE steps and prefill use the stock path.
- Startup refuses unsupported configs (default-deny), with every reason reported. Kernel faults fail-stop on every rank, and no token is returned from a failed step.
- Requirements: TP4 on gfx950, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`, `--moe-backend aiter`, `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`.
- Temporary dependency: imports the DeepSeek-V4.1 `mono.common` FlyDSL helpers (peer memory, sync), to move once a common AMD runtime lands.
### Results (MI355X, TP4, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs)
Baseline is the recommended serve command. `--monokernel` adds the flags it requires.
**Random 1024 in / 1024 out**
| Concurrency | Baseline TPOT (ms) | `--monokernel` TPOT (ms) | TPOT | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.12 | 4.27 | **−16.6%** | 192 → 230 (**+19.6%**) |
| 2 | 5.54 | 4.85 | **−12.5%** | 355 → 403 (+13.4%) |
| 4 | 6.23 | 5.69 | **−8.7%** | 628 → 687 (+9.3%) |
| 8 | 7.46 | 6.88 | **−7.8%** | 1054 → 1136 (+7.8%) |
| 16 | 8.89 | 8.87 | parity | 1755 → 1751 |
| 32 (stock fallback) | 11.51 | 11.54 | parity | 2684 → 2708 |

**Long context, 8192 in / 1024 out:** TPOT −14.9% at concurrency 1 (5.25 → 4.47 ms), −9.0% at 4 (6.42 → 5.84 ms), and −3.4% at 16 (10.12 → 9.78 ms).
**MT-Bench (chat, greedy, ≤1024 output tokens):** TPOT −17.0% at concurrency 1 (5.00 → 4.15 ms; 196 → 235 tok/s), −8.6% at 4 (6.30 → 5.76 ms), and parity at 16.
Kernel-only effect, against the same server with identical flags and no `--monokernel`: TPOT −19.1% at concurrency 1, −14.3% at 2, −11.1% at 4, −8.8% at 8, and parity at 16.

### Accuracy (GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319, flexible-extract)
| Config | Score |
|---|---|
| Same flags, no `--monokernel` | 0.8969 |
| `--monokernel` | 0.9052 (paired +0.83 pp, 95% CI [−0.83, +2.50], McNemar p=0.37) |

### Commands
Baseline:
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --block-size 128 --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --max-model-len 10240
```
`--monokernel`, which is the baseline plus:
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 ... \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --moe-backend aiter --monokernel
```
Benchmarks. Each point is preceded by a discarded warmup with a different seed. `--num-prompts` is max(32, 4×concurrency) for random and max(16, 4×concurrency) for MT-Bench.
```bash
# random
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code --backend vllm \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 1234 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
# MT-Bench
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path philschmid/mt-bench --skip-chat-template \
  --hf-output-len 1024 --temperature 0 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 1234
# accuracy
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,model=amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4,num_concurrent=4,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 1234
```
### Limitations / follow-ups
- Spec decoding is refused in this PR. The stock path is about 1.6× faster than `--monokernel` 
- TP4 only. TP2 and TP8 are follow-ups.
- At 16 rows the kernel is at parity

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fix HTTP 500 on long conversations: fuel-limit only request templates
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On the Rust frontend, long conversations fail with HTTP 500 even when the prompt is far below the context length (#62598). A GLM-5.3 agent session of 1,730 messages (21K tokens, about 2% of its 1M context) is rejected, while the same conversation renders in 0.12 s with transformers. Once a session reaches this point, every later request in it fails, and no setting raises the limit.

The cause is the hard-coded 500K MiniJinja instruction budget per render from #50300, which also applies to the model's own template. Since #62673, request-supplied templates are refused unless `--trust-request-chat-template` is set. This PR therefore keeps the budget for those templates only and renders the server's own template without one, as the Python frontend does. `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` overrides the request-template budget (`0` disables it), and the out-of-fuel error names it.

Fixes #62598

## Claims

- The server's own chat template renders without a fuel limit, so long conversations work by default. This matches the Python frontend, which has no instruction cap for it, only `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT`.
- Request-supplied templates, which only render with `--trust-request-chat-template`, keep the 500K budget from #50300, so the protection on that path is unchanged. `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` raises or disables it, and the out-of-fuel error says which variable to change, as the Python render-timeout error does. The variable is read once when the renderer is built, and an invalid value fails startup.

## Validation

Setup: `vllm-rs serve` + `vllm-mock-engine`, GLM-5.3 tokenizer and template, the repro from #62598 (one tool call and result per turn), `max_tokens=1`.

| build | serve flags | `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` | request | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `4e304b4d` | — | unset | server template, 1,730 msgs | 500 `engine ran out of fuel` |
| this PR | — | unset | server template, 1,730 / 3,002 msgs | 200 / 200 |
| this PR | — | unset | request template | 400, untrusted (from #62673) |
| this PR | `--trust-request-chat-template` | unset | request template, 1,728 / 1,730 msgs | 200 / 500, error names `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` |
| this PR | `--trust-request-chat-template` | `2000000` | request template, 1,730 msgs | 200 |

Tests:

- `only_request_templates_have_a_fuel_budget` renders a 20,000-message conversation with the default template, then shows that the same template runs out of fuel as a request template. It fails without the change.
- `test_long_conversation_exceeds_default_fuel` snapshots the error at the default budget.
- `test_raised_or_disabled_fuel_renders_long_conversation` covers a raised and a disabled budget.
- `test_chat_template_fuel_is_not_compile_factor` keeps the variable out of the compile cache key.

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-features --locked
pytest tests/test_envs.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py tests/test_envs.py rust/src/chat/src/renderer/hf/{error,mod,template}.rs  # also --hook-stage manual
```

All pass, except 6 tests that also fail on main on this machine: macOS grammar-replay snapshots, including `roundtrip_step5`, and a timing-sensitive audio test that passes on its own. Rendered output is unchanged, so no model eval.

## Details

- **Root cause.** Fuel counts executed instructions, and chat templates loop over messages. GLM-5.3's template spends about 290 instructions per message, so it reaches 500K at about 1,700 messages regardless of content length. #62598 measures the same limit at 1,682–21,740 messages across the templates in `examples/`.
- **No limit for the server's template.** That template is configured by the operator, through the model files or `--chat-template`. The Python frontend renders it without an instruction cap, and its cost grows with the request like tokenization does. If a cap is still wanted there, it is a one-line `with_fuel` on the default template.
- **Environment variable.** Like `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS`, it is declared in `vllm/envs.py` and read with `std::env::var`; `vllm-rs` inherits it when started from `vllm serve`. It is excluded from `compile_factors()`, since it does not affect compiled graphs.
- **Duplicates.** No existing PR covers this. I searched `fuel`, `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, `50300 in:body` and `52025 in:body`; the only hit, #60199, caps `tojson` indentation. #62673 adds the flag this builds on.
- **AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line, and the commands above were run locally.

commits.pr_title: [EPD] Support metadata-only audio-in-video requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support metadata-only `use_audio_in_video` requests for Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni in the Python EPD frontend/proxy.

## Claims

- Forward video timing and audio lengths without repeating media preprocessing on the consumer.
- Preserve both features' EC hashes and transfer handles; fall back to raw media for the whole request when metadata is incomplete.

## Validation

Original validation before the review fixes, GB200, 1E + 1PD, Model Runner V2: **48/48 functional smoke requests succeeded** across ECExample, Mooncake TCP, and CPU/NIXL with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B` and `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`.

Covered one/two videos with audio, image + video, and audio disabled, each repeated twice. Audio-enabled requests use `mm_processor_kwargs={"use_audio_in_video": true}`; both instances use `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`.

Review-fix validation:

- GB200, cached Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct weights, MRV2, eager mode, `enable_mm_embeds=True`, no EC connector: **4/4 synthetic embedding requests completed** (one/two images and one/two videos), followed by a successful text request on the same engine. Inputs used BF16 embeddings shaped `(4 * n, 8192)` with `grid_thw=[[1,4,4]] * n`; this checks request completion and item handling, not semantic accuracy. Runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.15.0, existing precompiled extensions.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passes the changed embedding-split path, then stops at the pre-existing `input_ids.cpu()` in Qwen3-Omni's `embed_input_ids`; the successful smoke above ran without that strict check. The full EPD connector matrix was not rerun for this follow-up.

## Details

A video with audio produces two encoder features. Carry both in one `video_embeds` content part with a companion `audio_embeds` payload and shared source UUID, preserving the chat template's single video item and interleaved placeholders.

Review fixes keep precomputed vision embeddings split by `grid_thw` in the shared Omni mixin. For push transfers, proxy-assigned IDs remain per occurrence even when encoder responses aggregate repeated hashes. Encoder response modalities select the audiovisual path; a single video feature uses the existing matching and raw-fallback behavior. Non-push connector-provided transfer handles remain supported.

Related: #52409. Duplicate checks found no equivalent PR; #57275 fixes raw-fallback identity and transfer lifecycle, not audiovisual metadata-only inputs.

## Overview

Require user-visible changes to ship with rendered docs, so users and agents can find what vLLM added. Adds a short "Documenting User-Visible Changes" section to `docs/contributing/README.md` (where each change type is documented, what to write first, and a findability check). `AGENTS.md` (3 lines) and `pr-checklist` §3.2 link to it instead of repeating it.

Fresh agents at the lowest reasoning effort, no prior context.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Fix INC ARK weight loading for small TP shards
commits.pr_body:
Issue: Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 INT4 AWQ fail on TP4 with tensor size mismatch 0 vs 2

Root cause: auto_round_kernel's QuantLinear preallocates buffers with floor-rounded shapes (e.g. qzeros width `out // 32 * bits`), which become 0 for narrow TP shards such as Qwen3.5 GDN in_proj_ba at TP=4, causing copy_() to fail with a shape mismatch.

Fixed: Assign the loaded qweight/qzeros/scales directly instead, since post_init() only relies on the actual tensor shapes.

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Use replace_parameter for params re-created in process_weights_after_loading
commits.pr_body:
**Depends on #62326; review only the last commit.**

## Overview

Part 2 of 3 of keeping the loaded parameter objects through `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL). With #62326, `replace_parameter` keeps the registered object. This PR converts the PWAL sites that still register a fresh `torch.nn.Parameter` over a loaded one to `replace_parameter`.

## Claims

- `layer.x = Parameter(...)`, `setattr(layer, x, Parameter(...))` and no-op rewraps (`Parameter(layer.x.data)`) in PWAL now go through `replace_parameter`, so the loaded object (class, `weight_loader`, dim attributes) survives. This covers:
  - linear kernels: MXFP4, MXFP6, MXFP8, NVFP4 (CUTLASS, FlashInfer, FBGEMM, PyTorch, Humming scales), mixed precision (ExLlama, RDNA3, XPU);
  - compressed-tensors, Quark, INC, FBGEMM FP8, ModelOpt, AutoAWQ and online lm_head methods, and Marlin FP4 helpers;
  - `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm`, CPU AMX MLA, and DeepSeek-V4 CPU attention.
- Coverage (whole-tree enumeration of PWAL-reachable sites on `main`, 1786 rows split across the three PRs): 141 sites converted here, plus 2 n/a rows inside the changed hunks. Deletes and renames in the same functions are left as on `main`; they are in the follow-up PR.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- On GB200, `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` and `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py` pass: 23 passed. This PR adds the `modelopt-fp8-pb-wo-linear` and `modelopt-mxfp8-linear` cases, which fail on #62326 alone.
- The end-to-end GB200 run is described in #62326. It compares `main`, #62326, and the top of the stack, which includes this PR. The rows that touch this PR's sites are below.

  | Config | GSM8K main / stack | Post-PWAL tensors |
  |---|---|---|
  | MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 (ModelOpt MXFP8 linear), TP4 | 0.859 / 0.859 | identical |
  | compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 per-tensor + FP8 KV cache | 0.738 / 0.738 | identical |
  | same, Humming forced (reads `processed_weight_dims`) | 0.751 / 0.758 | identical |
  | same, Marlin forced | 0.738 / 0.734 | identical |

  - The same kernels are selected in both arms.
  - Every loader-visible param is the same object after PWAL; on `main`, 10% are for W8A8 FP8 and 49% for M3.

## Details

- Compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 and ModelOpt FP8 per-tensor transpose the weight to (K, N). The kept param keeps its checkpoint dim tags, and the layout reaches Humming via `layer.processed_weight_dims` (added in #62326) instead of a retag.
- Where a site re-creates a param whose shape or dtype changes, `replace_parameter` rebinds `.data`; where the layout matches, it copies into the existing storage.
- `modelopt.py`, `quark_nvfp4.py`, `fbgemm_fp8.py`, `inc_wna16_linear.py` and `kernels/linear/nvfp4/humming.py` also delete or rename params. Only their `Parameter(...)` assignments are converted here.

commits.pr_title: [LoRA][Step5] Support LoRA for Step5
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds LoRA support to Step5 (`Step5ForCausalLM` and `Step5ForConditionalGeneration`), added in #61727.

## Claims

- LoRA on attention (`q/k/v/g_proj`), the sparse indexer projections, `sparse_indexer_w`, dense MLPs and routed experts (per-expert keys, via `FusedMoEWithLoRA`), for the text model and the VLM.
- `Step5FusedQKVIndexerWithLoRA` slices LoRA B for the seven fused slices with the layer's own offsets (KV and indexer replication included).
- `Step5SparseIndexerIndexTPLinear` becomes a `ColumnParallelLinear` with its logical index-TP rank/size, so `Step5SparseIndexerWWithLoRA` slices B like the weight loader. Non-LoRA loading is unchanged.

## Validation

GB300, `tests/lora/test_step5_lora.py` (run by the existing `lora` CI step). For every TP rank, the full weight is loaded through the layer's own weight loader, and the LoRA B slices must equal the loaded rows exactly. The fused layer's forward must also return the full `[qkv | indexer]` output.

| Tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main (a608b6e6) + new test | collection error: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm.lora.layers.step5'` |
| this PR | 13 passed (fused layer TP 1/2/4/8 × 1/4 indexer KV heads; `sparse_indexer_w` TP 1–16) |
| this PR without `apply = BaseLinearLayerWithLoRA.apply` | 2 failed (TP=1 drops the indexer half of the output) |

## Details

- `share_expert` is renamed with an idempotent regex. The VLM mapper and the text model mapper both apply it, and the old substring rule produced `.moe.moe.share_expert.`.
- LoRA is rejected with `moe_backend='deep_gemm_mega_moe'`: its experts are not `FusedMoE`, and its sequence-parallel mode gives the MLP linears `N/tp` tokens.
- `fully_sharded_loras` leaves these two layers without LoRA, like other custom linear subclasses.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Specialized decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

An opt-in specialized decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950), TP8, following RFC #60904. It uses the same `specialized_decode` shape as #61867 (Kimi-K3, NVIDIA) and #60889 (GLM-5.2, ROCm), in layer mode. It is enabled with `additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` and has no other options.

A pure spec-verify decode step of at most 8 rows runs each MoE decoder layer as persistent FlyDSL MonoKernels. The TP all-reduces run in-kernel over peer memory:

- **Whole layers** (68 KDA layers): K1 (AttnRes, in_proj, f_b, spec conv, KDA recurrence, gated RMSNorm), then K2.
- **FFN layers** (24 MLA layers): vLLM's AttnRes and MLA up to o_proj's input, then K2.
- **K2**: o_proj + all-reduce + MLP AttnRes, then the latent MoE (router, top-16 MXFP4 experts, shared experts, latent all-reduce + RMSNorm, up_proj, final all-reduce).

The kernels read vLLM's loaded weights and KDA states in place. Every other step (prefill, mixed, wider and PIECEWISE steps) runs vLLM's layers. With `decode_backend=auto` (the default) nothing changes.

### Layout: no common code

```text
vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/
    README.md        supported deployments, refusals, steps, fail-stop
    hooks.py         SpecializedDecodeMixin: the model-side hooks
    model_state.py   KimiK3ModelState: builds the executor after load, binds KV caches
    runtime/
        __init__.py  DecodeConfig, specialized_decode_config(), unsupported()
        decode.py    SpecializedDecode: plan() -> Step, Step.layer(i), prepare_kv(), after_step()
        guards.py    weight / KV cache refusals, fail-stop
        layers.py    layer kernels: vLLM tensors -> launches
        runner.py    per-rank launch state;  peer.py  peer memory, TP agreement
    mono/            kernel source (K1, K2, MoE stages, device primitives)
tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/
```

The existing Kimi-K3 files only call into the folder (26 added lines):
- `linear.py`: `specialized_decode_config()` in `__init__` before any module allocates weights, `plan_specialized_decode()` in `forward`, `(step.layer(i) or layer)(...)` in the layer loop, and `after_specialized_decode_step()` in `compute_logits`.
- `model.py`: `get_model_state_cls`.
- `mla.py`: `skip_o_proj`, which returns o_proj's input for the MLA layers' K2.

Outside `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` the only change is one Buildkite step.

### Refusal and steps

- **Refusal.** An unsupported deployment fails at startup with one `ValueError` that lists every reason. Refusals run in three stages: the config in `__init__`, the loaded weights when the model state builds the executor, and the KV caches at every bind. Every TP rank agrees on each verdict. It is default-deny for PP/DP/EP/EPLB/PCP, DBO, LoRA, KV connectors, routed-expert capture, sleep mode, CPU offload, weight updates, adaptive or dynamic speculative decoding, ReplaySSM/RecoverSSM, the V1 runner, `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`, other model shapes, and other GPUs or partitioned GPUs.
- **Steps.** `plan()` runs once per step. It picks the kernels for pure spec-verify steps of whole uniform requests at a built width, i.e. multiples of `k+1` up to 8 rows.
- **CUDA graphs.** vLLM's capture sizes are not changed. Under FULL graphs the plan is baked in at capture. A replay with fewer requests than its graph pads whole requests (null state slot, one accepted token), and the kernels serve those like real ones.

### Fail-stop

Every in-kernel wait gives up after 10 s. The rank records it in its sticky health words, so a stalled peer fails every rank instead of hanging them. In `compute_logits` each rank queues a non-blocking copy of its `FAILED` word. Every 16 steps the TP ranks agree on what has landed over the TP CPU group, and then every rank raises at the same step. This keeps all ranks out of the next collective.

Detection takes up to about 16 steps. A zero-delay check through a core hook can follow in a separate PR.

## Not a duplicate

- #61867 is Kimi-K3 on NVIDIA (CuTeDSL, SM100); this is the ROCm/FlyDSL counterpart under `kimi_k3/amd/`.
- #60397, #60889, #61482 and #60731 target other models (DeepSeek-V4.x, GLM-5.2), with different attention, residual and MoE.
- #61311 proposes shared abstractions. This PR keeps its runtime per model, as #61867 and #60889 do, and can move onto shared helpers once those land.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3          # 8x MI355X; includes amd_specialized_decode/
pre-commit run --files <changed files>     # incl. mypy
```

- **CPU:** the switch (auto / unknown value), widths, layer pattern, every refusal (one at a time, then all at once), PIECEWISE warning, cache refusal, step eligibility, `plan()` routing (PIECEWISE, too wide, prefill, PP input, unbound or re-bound KV cache), weight-view refusals.
- **GPU:** K1 against vLLM's KDA op chain; K2 at TP8 against o_proj + all-reduce + AttnRes + KimiMoE, with 300 bit-identical graph replays; a stalled rank finishes every launch and fails the step; warm-up compiles without launching.
- **Engine:** an 8-layer dummy K3 at TP8 stalls rank 3 inside a served decode step. A request fails, every rank raises at the same step, and the server exits.

Kimi-K3, TP8, DCP8, DSpark MTP, fp8 KV, `--stream-interval 10`, MI355X, FULL CUDA graphs, Model Runner V2. "Off" means the same image, tree and flags with `decode_backend=auto`.

## Test Result

This revision ran on 8x MI355X with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-1b2a6663`, which is 20 commits behind this branch's base with no `kimi_k3`, mamba, `gdn_attn` or model-state changes in between. This branch's `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` was mounted over the image.

- **pytest** `tests/models/kimi_k3`: **420 passed, 0 failed** (89 skipped). This covers the new suite and every existing Kimi-K3 test.
- **ISA:** all 17 production K1/K2 builds are byte-identical to the previous revision (df3693c), so the kernel results below carry over.
- **Startup refusal:** TP4 + V1 runner + no speculative decoding gives one `ValueError` with all three reasons. `decode_backend="fast"` is rejected.
- **8k/1k, c1, k=7, 3 seeds:** TPOT p50 5.44 → **4.31 ms (−20.8%)**, p90 5.48 → 4.35 ms, output 170.2 → 210.3 tok/s (+23.6%); the server logs `Kimi-K3 specialized decode: 92 layers, widths [8], 30 builds`.
- **GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 q:**
  - c1, k=7, on: 0.9651 ± 0.0051 (an earlier run of the same cell on this revision: 0.9538 ± 0.0058).
  - Padded replays (k=1, c3, vLLM's default capture sizes, so 3-request steps replay the 4-request graph): off 0.9621 vs on 0.9613 (±0.0053).

### Accuracy, previous revision (same kernels, ISA byte-identical)

The kernel path serves steps of at most 8 rows, so these configs fuse every decode step (conc x (k+1) <= 8):

| eval | config | off | on |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot | c4, k=1 | 0.9644 | 0.9629 / 0.9568 |
| GSM8K 5-shot | c2, k=3 | 0.9522 | 0.9568 |
| GSM8K 5-shot | c1, k=7 | 0.9598 | 0.9629 |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 q, CoT, 0-shot) | c4, k=1 | 0.9242 | 0.9394 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix multimodal sender-cache invalidation race with queued renders
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #62121. Apply sender-cache invalidations between generation renders on the single-worker multimodal executor so an engine cache-miss report cannot remove an entry between the processor's cache lookup and merge.

## Claims

- In-flight generation renders on the single-worker multimodal executor complete without the reported `Expected a cached item` assertion; already-queued renders consume pending invalidations before looking up cached data.
- Unrelated outputs keep flowing while multimodal processing or cache invalidation is blocked.
- Ignore uncached hashes and coalesce duplicate miss reports, avoiding unbounded notification growth on pre-rendered `features` traffic that never invokes the renderer.

## Validation

Current review cleanup (`20f04478`): both helpers return when the cache is absent; enqueue also returns for empty input or an empty filtered pending set. The output handler delegates empty-list handling to the helper while keeping its outer cache guard and enqueue-before-publish ordering.

- macOS arm64 CPU: `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/multimodal/test_cache.py tests/renderers/test_warmup.py tests/renderers/test_executor_replace.py -k "not sleep" -q` → **57 passed, 1 deselected**. The cleanup opt-out is described below; test assertions were unchanged.
- NVIDIA A800 80GB, Qwen2-VL-2B @ `895c3a49`: the unmodified `pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py::test_sleep_wake_preserves_mm_cache_consistency -s -vv -ra` → **1 passed, 0 skipped**. Logs confirm both generations and the intervening sleep/wake; sleep freed 38.05 GiB. Python sources were verified against `20f04478`; native artifacts were reused from official wheel `7b6310c1` with PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 / Transformers 5.19.0, and all model-file hashes matched the pinned revision.
- A real-renderer check with the invalidation lock held confirmed that empty lists, empty tuples and fully filtered hashes return without waiting or changing an existing pending invalidation. The next render resends the payload, and the following render hits the cache.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including ruff, format, typos, mypy, SPDX/import and configuration checks. `actionlint` was excluded because its local environment could not initialize; no workflow files changed. `git diff --check` passed.

The offline processor performance measurements compare `a0e7137c` with `d2097ba5`, not this cleanup: [initial benchmark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62164#issuecomment-6262374327), [three-repeat 1,024-prompt results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62164#issuecomment-6283546827). These synchronous measurements do not cover async miss-notification contention.

Coalescing implementation (`d2097ba5`), earlier macOS arm64 CPU validation, Python 3.13.15 / PyTorch 2.14.1:

- `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -k "not sleep" -q`: **29 passed, 1 deselected**. Includes LRU, SHM/IPC, the original forced-interleaving regression, coalescing/clear behavior, and a multi-hash failure with concurrent notifications.
- `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/renderers/test_warmup.py tests/renderers/test_executor_replace.py -q`: **28 passed**.
- The local `pytest_skipgc` plugin applies the repository's `skip_global_cleanup` marker to avoid the previously observed macOS torch teardown crash; it does not modify test assertions. SHM tests ran with local shared-memory access enabled.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, format, typos, mypy and Buildkite test tethering. `actionlint` was skipped; no workflow file changed. `git diff --check` passed.
- A method-level comparison using the real renderer/processor/LRU cache and the submitted `dc1a962` queue/drain methods reproduced the backlog: 1,000 absent hashes retained 1,000 records before and 0 after; 200 notifications for one cached hash retained 200 before and 1 after. The next render resent the payload in both cases. This was not a full baseline-tree pytest run.

The original assertion regression previously failed on pristine `a0e7137c` and passed on submitted commit `dc1a962`. That submitted implementation also has Linux CPU validation (27 passed, 1 deselected) and A800 serving evidence below. **The historical HTTP stress measurements below remain specific to `dc1a962`. The `d2097ba5` offline benchmarks and `20f04478` sleep/wake test do not replace a rerun of that HTTP stress workload.**

<details>
<summary>Historical A800 serving comparison for submitted commit dc1a962</summary>

Qwen2-VL-2B @ 895c3a49, A800 80GB PCIe, localhost HTTP using the reporter's pause/resume plus background-image load, no server-side hook. Five-minute trigger and two-minute control per arm:

| arm | rounds | target asserts | image requests | ok | other 500 | stream errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main trigger | 164 | 18 | 32,138 | 31,794 | 196 | 130 |
| dc1a962 trigger | 164 | 0 | 31,934 | 31,565 | 199 | 170 |
| main control | 56 | 0 | 24,632 | 24,632 | 0 | 0 |
| dc1a962 control | 56 | 0 | 25,070 | 25,070 | 0 | 0 |

Twelve fixed public-image responses were byte-identical for text, finish reason and completion-token count. Remaining errors were the existing P1-miss class; internal-error lines increased from 344 to 369 (1.07% to 1.16%). No overall error-rate improvement is claimed.

</details>

## Details

The output handler previously invalidated the sender cache on the asyncio thread while the renderer performed its lookup and merge on its single-worker multimodal executor.

The handler now records missed hashes before publishing the associated outputs. Only hashes currently present in the sender cache are retained. When a processor cache is present, a short lock protects a pending set; each render swaps that set before its first lookup. Both helpers return immediately when there is no cache. Enqueue also returns for empty input or when filtering leaves no live hashes, before acquiring the lock. Membership checks and cache invalidation execute outside the lock. Failed invalidation restores the current and remaining hashes without discarding newly arrived notifications. Cache clear retains its existing behavior; stale notifications become no-ops at the next render boundary.

This avoids a second executor job and queue/set mirrored state. Pending records can briefly outlive the cache entry they reference, so this does not claim that their count always equals the instantaneous live cache size. Sync LLM retains direct invalidation.

This is distinct from #34749's assertion-to-error conversion and #61656's endpoint retries. P1 drift itself, automatic HTTP retries, and #62123's SHM handle issue are out of scope. The [pre-existing pooling/embedding cross-executor race](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62164#discussion_r4311154000) is also not addressed by this fix. The issue came from a public report and was investigated with constructed reproductions; it was not encountered in the submitter's production workload. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation and validation, including this follow-up review.

## Overview

Capture offload event metadata on `HIT_PENDING` so KVCR inventory arriving before primary delivery has real tokens, hashes and geometry—not a zero-size FullAttention placeholder that triggers quarantine.

## Claims

- Preserve pending lookup status; do not announce a native store early.
- Hold metadata for allocated primary slots, including secondary-only residency.
- Clean up failed primary allocations without public evictions or deleting retry metadata.

## Validation

- Updated standalone CPU suites: **100 passed, 4 deselected**; new shared-prefix and retry regressions fail without their fixes.

## Details

KVCR can announce committed G2 inventory before primary delivery completes. Capture the payload while the primary slot exists but is not yet readable; use internal failed-allocation cleanup and discard stale cleanup when a retry already owns the key.

Independent of #59703 and ai-dynamo/dynamo#15535. Unlike provenance redesign #52103, this backfills KVCR inventory through the existing tracker. Consumer validation is unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Nemotron Parse 3.5 serving and MTP support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds native serving for Nemotron Parse 3.5's causal visual-prefix architecture and a one-token auxiliary MTP proposer. This extends the Parse model implementation; related earlier-model speculative work is [#51168](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51168).

## Claims

- Register RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and process variable-resolution packed RADIO images with content-normalized positional embeddings and visual-prefix placeholder expansion.
- Add ParseAuxMTPModel, loading the checkpoint's integrated auxiliary projections and routing causal-prefix configurations to one speculative token on Model Runner V2.
- Extend HF/vLLM generation coverage to Parse 3.5 and add five MTP configuration/loading/sharing contract tests to Basic Models CI. End-to-end MTP correctness and speedup remain unvalidated.
- Older generations of Nemotron-Parse are still supported.

## Validation

Tests ran locally. The nemotron-3.5-parse (with and without mtp) and nemotron-parse-2.0 accuracy verified on internal benchmarks. Parse 3.5 mtp acceptance rate is verified at various concurrencies. Tested on A100, H100. 

## Details

New nemotron-3.5-parse model uses an updated architecture which the current vllm implementation does not support. To simplify the change, created a new nemotron_parse3_5.py implementation while leaving code for previous versions unchanged. Major differences compared to previous implementation and approaches taken for implementations: 
1. New model uses visual prefix and removes cross-attention. 
add_cross_attention field controls whether to add cross-attention in decoder layer. Parse 3.5 implementation in vllm only supports checkpoints that has it set to False (as official checkpoint). Added a hard fail check that nemotron-3.5-parse models have it set to False. 
2. New model uses GQA vs old model using MHA.
Since WhisperAttention does not support GQA, created a local attention implementation that copies Whisper but adds GQA support. Can instead add GQA support to Whisper, but this increases common-code change. 
3. New model uses dynamic-size vision encoder with packed batching (NaVit-style) vs old model using static resolution. 
New RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and pre-processing. Parse 3.5 is not using device-side preprocessing for parse 3.5 for simplicity (d1d8e6c). 
4. New model uses a different version of RADIO encoder.
Added RADIOv4-SO400M parameters to RADIO file. Model: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/C-RADIOv4-SO400M

## Known limitations and future work

1. Only V2 runner is supported for mtp-enabled parse 3.5. V1 runner fails because it expects kv-cache in the speculator and parse mtp does not have attention. 
2. RADIO dynamic packing causes a sync on . This code is reused between models, so leaving it as-is for this PR. The torch.tensor constructor should be replaced with async copy in the future. Will submit separate PR. 
3. Nemotron-3.5-Parse is currently not public, so the 3.5-specific tests are disabled. Those tests and additional validation for parse 3.5 was ran locally.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Optimize Molmo2 pooling preparation
commits.pr_body:
### Purpose

Molmo2 pooling currently materializes a tiled batch-index tensor and uses
multi-dimensional advanced indexing before masking invalid patches and reducing
the attention query.

This change keeps the implementation in native PyTorch while reducing that
overhead. It flattens the batch-local patch indices into global row indices,
uses `torch.index_select` for the gather, masks invalid entries in place, and
performs the existing sum/mean query reduction without changing the subsequent
attention, projection, or token filtering behavior.

No Triton kernel or custom-op dispatch is added, so there is no extra JIT
startup cost or platform-specific fallback path.

### Tests and validation

Pooling coverage is consolidated into the existing
`tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py` suite. Two parametrized
cases exercise `Molmo2VisionBackbone.forward` with lightweight substitutes
for the encoder and learned layers, checking masked and ordinary means,
partially/all-invalid groups, repeated indices, cross-batch indexing, attention
masks, and invalid-group filtering against explicit expected values.

The standalone 228-line pooling test file and benchmark script have been
removed. The pooling implementation is unchanged by this review follow-up.

Agent-run on macOS 15.1 ARM64, Python 3.12.13 and PyTorch 2.14.0, from the
PR worktree using the parent checkout's virtual environment:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 ../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py
# 7 passed; one existing warning about missing vllm._version

../../.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/molmo2.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy

git diff --check
# Passed
```

The suite uses the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker because these CPU
unit tests do not initialize distributed or accelerator state. Without it,
the existing processing tests triggered a macOS/PyTorch
`empty_host_cache` teardown crash in the local environment.

### RTX 4090 Microbenchmark (historical)

The script is preserved at [the pre-follow-up commit](https://github.com/Levius-Fubuki/vllm/blob/e26ed1564398652949f446d78fa252eac26b40a2/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_molmo2_pooling.py); the command below refers to that version. These measurements were not rerun for this test-only follow-up.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_molmo2_pooling.py \
  --batch-sizes 1 2 \
  --dtypes float16 bfloat16 \
  --warmup 50 --repeats 200 --trials 10
```

Hardware/software: NVIDIA RTX 4090, PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130, Triton 3.7.1.

The benchmark compares the exact upstream native preparation path against the
optimized native helper. Across 24 image/video rows, every measured case
improved. The geometric-mean speedup was 1.29x, with a range of 1.06x--1.50x.

| B | kind | dtype | groups | Upstream median / IQR (us) | Optimized median / IQR (us) | Speedup |
|---:|:---|:---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | image K=4 | FP16 | 550 | 165.55 / 0.17 | 118.42 / 0.34 | 1.40x |
| 1 | video K=9 | FP16 | 256 | 175.82 / 13.33 | 117.49 / 0.82 | 1.50x |
| 1 | video K=9 | BF16 | 4096 | 991.10 / 0.44 | 927.38 / 0.53 | 1.07x |
| 2 | video K=9 | FP16 | 4096 | 1954.28 / 5.32 | 1830.80 / 0.18 | 1.07x |


### Limitations

The performance measurements isolate pooling preparation rather than full-model
end-to-end latency. This follow-up was validated against the PR source with local
Python dependencies and no built vLLM native extensions. CUDA tests, full-model
evaluation and benchmarks were not rerun; GPU evidence above is historical.
The new validation results are agent-run, not human-run.

### AI assistance

AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, benchmarking, review,
and PR drafting. I reviewed and take responsibility for the change and
evidence.

commits.pr_title: [CPU] Improve long-context MTP attention scheduling on AMX
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

# [CPU] Improve long-context MTP attention scheduling on AMX

## Purpose

Extend CPU attention's grouped-query (GQA) scheduling to eligible
causal multi-token requests, including MTP verification and short prefill. The
existing batch-level GQA fast path requires an all-q1 decode batch, so these
requests do not receive the same grouped scheduling. The scheduler evaluates
grouped query heads and split-KV work using each request's query length,
causality, and AMX geometry, then selects a plan through its cost model. This
applies with auto, FP8 E4M3, and FP8 E5M2 KV cache.

## Duplicate-work Check

PR [#46154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46154) is related but not
a duplicate. It fixes generic mixed-batch GQA decode classification when
split-KV can divide a prefill request into one-token work items. This change
adds request-level eligibility based on causality, prefill state, and
verification query length, and uses it to enable AMX speculative multi-token
GQA scheduling with BF16 attention and FP8 KV.

Issue [#46131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46131), its comments,
open PRs referencing the issue, and open PRs matching CPU attention/GQA/spec
decode terms were checked. #46154 was the relevant overlap found.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -P -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py
.venv/bin/python -P -m pytest -s -v \
  tests/evals/mrcr/test_mrcr_correctness.py \
  --config-list-file="$MRCR_CONFIG_LIST"
```

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 128K \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# In another terminal:
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 100000 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 1 --num-warmups 1 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 1000
```

Serving uses BF16 TP1, batch size 1, and no prefix caching. The original
comparison also used auto KV with and without MTP3. The MRCR configs use the
existing 40-sample inputs and thresholds with three speculative tokens. Set
`MRCR_CONFIG_LIST` to the auto-KV or FP8-KV config list for each evaluation.

## Test Result

Serving used 100k input/1k output tokens with zero failures. Main
`6b24bd8e75a3` values are medians of three timed requests. Auto-KV branch
`65e9381658fe` values are also three-request medians; FP8 branch
`59b2f5f7b4` is one timed request after one warmup, built from the same source
state just before that commit. The FP8 fix leaves auto-KV scheduler selection
unchanged.

| Configuration | Main output tok/s | Branch output tok/s | Main TPOT (ms) | Branch TPOT (ms) | Main TTFT (s) | Branch TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No MTP, auto KV | 6.73 | 7.08 | 79.29 | 75.49 | 71.04 | 67.39 |
| MTP3, auto KV | 8.01 | 9.48 | 48.72 | 34.33 | 77.99 | 72.88 |

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Build] Compile paged attention kernels in parallel (7.6x faster attention build)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

`csrc/rocm/attention.cu` is a single 3.9k-line translation unit whose kernel instantiation is the tail of the ROCm build: ~9 min of a ~10.5 min build, on one core. This inflation was probably especially caused by recent: #42755  (adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` as a template parameter to all 12 kernels = interleaved + non-interleaved instantiation (+50%))

This PR splits the instantiations into one translation unit per (dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size) combination so ninja builds them in parallel.

*Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this (searched issues and PRs for `attention.cu` split / translation unit / ROCm compile time / `MAX_JOBS`). The closest open items are #17419 (general "builds are too slow" RFC) and #60906 (reuse the CMake build dir for editable installs); both are orthogonal to removing the single-TU bottleneck.*

## Claims

- Attention kernel compile drops from **547 s on 1 core to 72 s on 12 cores** (7.6×); the full editable install from ~10 min 40 s to ~1 min 35 s.
- `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link drops from ~2 s to 0.26 s (it no longer waits behind one 9-minute object).
- No behavior change: identical template instantiations, identical dispatch order, unchanged `paged_attention` signature and op registration.
- Cost: `_rocm_C.abi3.so` grows 196.3 MB → 219.2 MB (+11.6%) and aggregate CPU work grows ~30%, both traded for the 7.6× wall-clock win.

**How the file got this big.** The instantiation matrix was grown one axis at a time:

| PR | landed | what it added | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| #8310 | 2024-09-13 | initial ROCm custom paged attention | 1,038 lines, 4 kernels; already `{fp16,bf16}` × head `{64,128}` × block `{16,32}` × alibi `{on,off}` |
| #8577 | 2024-09-19 | fp8 KV cache | adds the `KV_DTYPE`/`cache_t` axis (fp8, `kFp8E4M3`) |
| #12348 | 2025-03-04 | "Faster Custom Paged Attention" rewrite | 4 → 6 kernels (`mfma16`, `mfma4`, partition `reduce`), +1,084/−422 |
| #17139 | 2025-05-07 | FP8 output fusion | `if (fp8_out_scale) → OUTT=uint8_t` = ×2 |
| #17004 | 2025-05-21 | RDNA/NAVI support on v1 | duplicates the kernel set for gfx11/gfx12, 6 → 12 `__global__`, ≈×2, +1,880/−171 |
| #22222 | 2025-09-15 | fp8 paged attention update | adds `MFMAType` (`Fp8` vs `F16`) = ×2 on the fp8 path |
| #42755 | 2026-10-15 | Qwen3-30B QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion | adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` to all 12 kernels = +50% |

Cumulative, per architecture: 6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × head (2) × block (2) × fp8-out (2) × alibi (2) × {NAVI, non-NAVI, interleaved} ≈ 288 launcher instantiations → ~860 device kernels in one file. `--offload-arch` values are additionally compiled serially inside that file, so release builds covering `gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950` pay ~3× the per-architecture cost.


## Validation

Compile times on MI350 in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1` with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950`; no compiler flags were set by hand, `-O2 -g` comes from the default `RelWithDebInfo` build type:

| Step | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| attention kernel compile (wall) | 547 s on 1 core | 72 s on 12 cores (58–72 s per TU) |
| `attention_dispatch.cu` (now the dispatch TU only) | — | 15 s |
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link | ~2 s | 0.26 s |
| full `MAX_JOBS=64 pip install -vvv -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation` | 10 min 40 s | 1 min 35 s |
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` size | 196.3 MB | 219.2 MB |

Per-edge timings come from `.ninja_log` of a cold build (`CCACHE_DISABLE=1 ninja -j64 _rocm_C`); all 12 attention TUs start within 2 ms of each other and finish 58–72 s later, so the split parallelizes as intended.

Kernel correctness — the positive matrix covers head 64/128 × block 16/32 × fp16/bf16 × kv auto/fp8 × alibi on/off × interleaved-V on/off × GQA 1/4/8, i.e. every one of the 12 instantiation TUs:

```bash
# f16 MFMA path (default)
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k num_heads0 -q
# 128 passed, 256 deselected, 414 s

# fp8 MFMA path (*_fp8_fp8 TUs)
VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1 python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k "num_heads0 and fp8" -q
# 64 passed, 320 deselected, 206 s

# head-size `default:` branch of the dispatch
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention_unsupported_head_sizes -q
# 7 passed, 1 s
```

No model eval is included: the split does not change kernels, dispatch, or numerics, only how many objects they are compiled into.

**Left for other PRs** (no automated coverage today, unchanged by this PR):
- [ ] Block-size `default:` of `ATTN_LAUNCH` (`Unsupported block size: `): `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` returns `MultipleOf(16)`, so `block_size=64` does reach the op — needs a `test_paged_attention_unsupported_block_sizes` analogue of the head-size test.
- [ ] `*_fp8_fp8` TUs in CI: only run here via `VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1`, and no `.buildkite/` or `.github/` job sets it; parametrizing a subset over `mfma_type in {"f16", "fp8"}` would cover them.
- [ ] `fp8_out_scale` (`OUTT=uint8_t`, doubles the instantiations in every TU): no test references it.
- [ ] `kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3"` alias handled in `attention_dispatch.cu`: untested.
- [ ] Compile-test the NAVI regions with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx1100;gfx1201"`: the `__HIP__GFX9__`/NAVI `#if` blocks are now evaluated once per file and were only exercised on MI350.

## Details

**Root cause.** A HIP translation unit is compiled by one clang process on one core; there is no clang equivalent of `nvcc --threads`, and additional `--offload-arch` values are also processed serially inside that process. `attention.cu` instantiates 12 kernels across 6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × 2 head sizes × 2 block sizes × alibi on/off × fp16/fp8 output × 2 v-cache layouts × CDNA/NAVI, so the whole tail is one serial 9-minute compile that `MAX_JOBS=64` cannot help with. (The popular "`Linking _moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` is slow" symptom is a ninja progress artifact: the link is 159 ms and the following line is simply not printed until `attention.hip.o` finishes.)

**Why splitting helps, measured.** Compile time is linear in the number of instantiations: restricting head size to 64 (half the instantiations) gives 270 s vs 547 s for the full set. So distributing the instantiations over N TUs gives ~N× wall-clock, minus a fixed cost.

**Why not just drop debug info.** Building the same TU with `-g0` gives 451 s vs 547 s, i.e. `-g` is only ~18% of the cost, and it would change the shipped build type. Splitting removes 475 s while keeping `RelWithDebInfo`.

**Design.** `csrc/rocm/attention_kernels.cuh` (renamed from `attention.cu`) holds the device helpers, all kernel and launcher templates, and the parameter-list macro. Each `csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_<head>_<dtype>_<kv>.cu` is ~4 lines: it includes the header and instantiates one combination via `ATTN_LAUNCH(...)`, exposing a fixed-head-size entry point. `csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu` keeps `is_navi_gpu()` and the dtype/kv-cache dispatch (unchanged order) and forwards to those entry points. The instantiation sets are disjoint, so nothing is compiled twice on purpose. hipify follows quoted includes, so the new header is hipified like any other (`attention_kernels_hip.cuh`) and no build-system special-casing is needed beyond listing the new `.cu` files in `VLLM_ROCM_EXT_SRC`. Renaming `attention.cu` to `attention_kernels.cuh` keeps the 3.9k moved lines recorded as a rename, so `git blame`/`--follow` survive.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- `.so` grows 196.3 → 219.2 MB (+11.6%), and the extra is debug info, not code: `.hip_fatbin` carries the device DWARF, and each TU emits its own copy of it for the headers/types it includes (the split's objects total 207.6 MB vs 169.4 MB, of which `.hip_fatbin` is 188.8 MB with `-g` but 42.2 MB with `-g0`, i.e. the ISA does not duplicate). Building these TUs with `-g1` gives a 96.1 MB `.so` and `-g0` a 74.9 MB one, both well below `main`'s 196.3 MB; that is left out here because it changes shipped debug info for the ROCm kernels, so it belongs in its own PR (there is exactly one out-of-line device helper, `warpReduceMax`, so marking helpers `__forceinline__` recovers nothing).
- Adding a head size, dtype, or kv-cache combination now means adding a TU and a `CMakeLists.txt` entry; the comments in `attention_kernels.cuh` and `CMakeLists.txt` point at this.
- The split is unbalanced: head size 128 TUs take ~70 s vs ~59 s for head size 64. Splitting within head size 128 (e.g. by block size) would lower the 72 s further, but the floor is ~20 s of frontend parsing per TU (measured with `-fsyntax-only`), so gains beyond 12–24 TUs are small unless a precompiled header is added.
- `attention_kernels.cuh` is hipified (`attention_kernels_hip.cuh`) like the ~15 other headers already in the tree (`quant_utils.cuh` → `quant_utils_hip.cuh`, `layernorm_utils.cuh`, …). `hipify_all` is an `add_custom_target` with no output file, so ninja treats it as always dirty and re-runs hipify on every build (~1 s), which regenerates those headers; editing the source header is therefore re-hipified normally and picked up by the next compile.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Include KV cache quantization settings in IPC weight cache key
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix incorrect KV scales when an engine reuses IPC-cached weights prepared with a different KV cache quantization configuration.

Related to #56049

## Claims

- Detect incompatible KV cache dtype or skipped-layer settings through the existing cache mismatch and fallback handling.
- Retain the KV cache configuration used during initial loading for subsequent standalone weight reloads.

## Validation

Added one parameterized regression test covering dtype mismatches, skipped-layer mismatches, and equivalent skipped-layer lists. It checks initial loading and standalone reloading, including after the caller's configuration is mutated.

- Before: **2 failed, 1 passed**.
- After: **9 passed, 3 deselected**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py \
  -k 'not cold_start_and_warm_restart' -q
```

GPU validation used an H800 NVL, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu130`, and a synthetic FP8 checkpoint derived from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, with BF16 activations, TP=1, eager execution, and the Torch FP8 linear backend. Three prompts were tested with greedy decoding, 32 output tokens, and prompt logprobs.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Before: `auto` daemon → `fp8` engine | Incorrectly accepted cached weights; K/V scales became `1.0` instead of `0.0250244140625`, changing generated tokens for all three prompts |
| After: mismatch, fallback disabled | Raised `CacheConfigMismatchError` naming `kv_cache_dtype` |
| After: mismatch, fallback enabled | Both `zero_copy` and `copy` matched disk loading |
| After: matching `fp8` configurations | Both modes loaded 424 cached tensors and matched disk loading |

For matching configurations and fallback loading, KV scales, generated token IDs, and prompt logprobs matched disk loading exactly. Disk-loading results were unchanged by the fix. These checks validate loading consistency for the tested FP8 path, not model accuracy or all quantization backends.

## Details

The daemon caches tensors after weight processing, which depends on the KV cache configuration. The existing fingerprint includes model quantization settings but omits the KV cache dtype and skipped layers, allowing incompatible processed scales to be reused.

Include `kv_cache_dtype` and `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` in `WeightCacheKey`. Sort and deduplicate skipped layers so equivalent lists still match.

Pass `CacheConfig` when constructing daemon and engine keys. Save a copy on models returned by the IPC loader, including disk fallback, so standalone `load_weights()` calls retain the configuration used during initial loading without requiring an active configuration context. Models without a saved configuration use the current vLLM configuration.

---

commits.pr_body:
- Set the test helper's `_results_ready` event from the results queue's `put()` instead of inside `batch_lookup()` in `test_async_lookup.py`

`test_found_key_returns_true` fails intermittently with `assert None is True` (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95734 on `main`, and https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95743). The helper set the event inside `batch_lookup()`, while `AsyncLookupManager`'s worker only posts the results to `_pending_results` after `batch_lookup()` returns, so a test waking in between drains an empty queue and `lookup()` still returns `None`. commits.pr_title: [XPU][Attention] Route multimodal prefix masks through the Triton/FlashAttention composite
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On XPU, multimodal prefix-LM models (Gemma 3/4) run Triton attention for every batch: the SYCL FlashAttention kernel cannot apply the image mask, and `Gemma4Config` forces `TRITON_ATTN` when FA4 is unavailable. Only image batches need the mask; text prefill and decode pay for Triton for nothing (3–4× slower per attention call than SYCL FlashAttention on Arc Pro B70).

Reuse the Triton/FlashAttention composite from #56305: image-masked batches → Triton, causal batches → FlashAttention, shared KV cache.

- `FlashAttentionBackend.supports_head_size`: allow ≤ 512 on XPU (SYCL kernels support 512; Gemma 4 global layers).
- `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` composite: FA3/FA4 and Hopper requirements apply to CUDA only (`device_major` moved into the FA route's `supports_compute_capability`; CUDA selection unchanged).
- `platforms/xpu.py`: select the composite for mm-prefix models with head size 256/512 and bf16/fp16 when no backend is requested; float32 or other head sizes fall back to Triton.
- `Gemma4Config`: no longer forces `TRITON_ATTN` on XPU. Side effect: with multimodal disabled, Gemma 4 defaults to FlashAttention.

No kernel changes.

## Test Plan

- Backend selection checked on XPU: composite for head 256/512 with image mask; Triton for head 128 and float32; FlashAttention without image mask. No unit test in this PR.
- 4× Arc Pro B70, TP=4, `--enforce-eager`, vLLM 0.32.0rc1 nightly: Gemma-4-26B-A4B text-only prefill (16 × 2048) and decode (bs32, 128/256) with `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` vs new default; Gemma-4-31B greedy outputs on image and text prompts, both backends.
- Not covered: graph mode, mixed image+text batches.

## Test Result

- Text-only 26B: prefill 8.9k → 11.8k tok/s (+32 %), decode 385 → 576 tok/s (+50 %).
- Images, 31B: composite selected (`TRITON_FLASH_ATTN`, block 64); 4/7 greedy outputs identical to Triton-only, the rest diverge after 21–47 identical tokens (within TP=4 run-to-run variation); 21.9 s → 16.6 s for the set.
- Decode traces: Triton attention 283 µs (26B) / 399 µs (31B) per call at bs64 vs ~60 / 95 µs SYCL FlashAttention; with graphs, FlashAttention is 25–41 % faster end to end at bs32–64 on 26B.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][MoE] Add platform hook for routed-expert capture rows
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add `Platform.get_routed_experts_local_rows` so out-of-tree MoE backends can restore their routing rows without replacing the shared capturer. This is a deliberately smaller alternative to #62441 for #61539.

Follow-up commits `ccb5f10`, `a43477b` and `27324c6` refine the change: the hook docstring covers stream/graph requirements and the MRV2 aux-output wiring, `docs/design/plugin_system.md` lists the optional hook, and the fallback test exercises the default TP gather. The capturer deliberately performs no validation of platform results; the buffer write is the contract.

## Claims

- A platform can return logical expert IDs in local token order, including an empty tensor. Only `None` selects the existing generic DP/TP restoration.
- Router selection and capture callback signatures, default restoration, and the capture-before-EPLB ordering remain unchanged.

## Validation

- **Linux regression, H20 cluster** (SGP H20e, 1x H20-3e on `vllm-sgp-h20-01`): exact base wheel `vllm-0.32.1rc1.dev118+g3897f95cf` from `wheels.vllm.ai`, with this PR's two production files overlaid onto the wheel:
  `pytest --import-mode=importlib -p no:cacheprovider -q --confcutdir=tests/model_executor tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`
  -> **55 passed in 19.26s** (`vllm 0.32.1rc1.dev118+g3897f95cf`, `torch 2.13.0+cu130`).
  Caveat: the shared H20 venv carries torch 2.13.0 while the wheel metadata pins 2.14.0. The module is CPU-only and imports/runs cleanly, but a torch-2.14 run remains outstanding.
- **Ruff 0.14.0** (the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: PASS.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- CI `pre-commit`, `DCO` and test-tethering checks: PASS.
- Not validated: accelerator collectives, graph replay, downstream Ascend integration. The hook's collective path is only exercised by downstream platforms (tracked separately).

## Details

Some out-of-tree MoE prepare implementations transform the routing input before expert selection. Generic inference from row counts cannot recover uneven TP shards or padding inside shards reliably. The platform already owns the communication/layout details and can normalize the routing rows through this hook.

The default returns `None`. The capturer passes the forward context, DP rank and TP size, accepts platform results without evaluating tensor truthiness, and assigns them to the capture buffer. The interface documents token order, empty results, stream/graph requirements and collective participation. The hook itself introduces no device synchronization or tensor value reads.

**Alternative design and duplicate-work check:** #62441 addresses the same use case through explicit layout objects, shared gather/select logic, and changes to both router implementations. This proposal intentionally keeps those signatures intact and adds a single platform normalization seam instead. The tradeoff is that platform-specific gathering and row selection remain the platform's responsibility rather than a common declarative executor. These are competing designs for #61539, not two independently needed fixes; they should be evaluated as alternatives. Searches for `61539 in:body`, routed-expert layouts, and the hook name found #62441 and no existing Platform-hook implementation PR. The alternative is explained in [the RFC discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61539#issuecomment-6284702593).

The production diff touches only the Platform interface and capturer. Existing tests are extended with multi-element, empty, zero-valued and fallback-padding cases. Downstream Ascend integration is separate and is not included or claimed as working here.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, tests and this description.
